# 🛡️ PhishGuard

**AI-Based Phishing Website Detection and Risk Analysis System Using Machine Learning**

PhishGuard tells you whether a website is likely to be a phishing site, and why. It reads the URL with four trained machine-learning models (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and SVM, with the best one, Random Forest, driving the score). At the same time it runs 50+ live checks on the domain, the certificate, the page and local threat-intelligence feeds, and it combines everything into a **0-100 risk score** with a **Legitimate / Suspicious / Phishing** verdict and the reasons behind it. A React dashboard, a documented REST API and a Chrome extension all use the same engine. The dashboard adds analytics, a model-comparison lab, monitoring and community reporting.

> 🎓 **B.Tech mini project** by **Ayushi Tiwari**, under the guidance of **Mr. Vishal Gupta**. Department of Computer Science & Engineering, Lloyd Institute of Engineering & Technology, Greater Noida. Affiliated to Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow.

> [!NOTE]
> The live demo runs in **demo mode** on a bundled snapshot of demo data. Anything you add (scans, reports, watchlist items) is reset when the serverless function restarts, and watchlist checks run once a day through a Vercel Cron job. Run it locally for the full experience.

## 📖 About the project

### Problem statement

Phishing websites copy real login, banking and payment pages to steal usernames, passwords and card details. A good copy is hard to tell from the real site, and checking a URL by hand needs technical knowledge that most users do not have. Blocklists help, but a phishing site set up this morning is usually not on any list yet, and many phishing pages are taken down again within hours.

PhishGuard addresses this by **learning what phishing URLs look like**. It extracts features from the URL, scores them with trained machine-learning models, and backs the prediction with live checks of the website itself: domain age, DNS, the SSL certificate, redirects, login forms, brand look-alikes and threat-intelligence feeds. Every URL is classified as **Legitimate**, **Suspicious** or **Phishing**, with a 0-100 risk score and the reasons behind it.

### Objectives

Condensed from the project synopsis:

| # | Objective | How PhishGuard meets it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Detect phishing websites with machine learning, by analysing their URLs and related characteristics | A trained classifier scores every URL, and live website checks add evidence the URL alone cannot show |
| 2 | Build a reliable labelled dataset of legitimate and phishing URLs | **146,364 URLs** (73,241 phishing, 73,123 legitimate) from PhiUSIIL, PhishTank, Phishing.Database, OpenPhish, the Tranco list and public sitemaps |
| 3 | Extract meaningful URL features | **44 lexical features**: lengths, dots, hyphens, `@`, digits, sub-domains, entropy, suspicious keywords and TLDs, shorteners, IP hosts, punycode, brand tricks and more |
| 4 | Pre-process the data for classification | De-duplication, at most 3 URLs per phishing campaign, identical URL normalisation, a group-aware 80/20 split (no domain in both train and test), feature scaling where the model needs it |
| 5 | Train and compare **Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and SVM** | All four are trained and evaluated on the same split and compared on accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and ROC-AUC on the Model Lab page |
| 6 | Select the best model | **Random Forest** has the highest test F1 (0.856, accuracy 86.4%, ROC-AUC 0.945) and drives the score |
| 7 | Classify each URL as **Legitimate / Suspicious / Phishing** | Verdict thresholds at risk 35 and 65 (adjustable in Settings) |
| 8 | Give a clear risk indication | 0-100 risk score, trust score, five reputation tiers, threat type, and positive and negative factors in plain English |
| 9 | Provide a simple interface where users enter a URL and see its status | A React dashboard: paste a link on the Scan page and get the full report in a few seconds |

### Scope

**In scope**

- Phishing detection for any `http://` or `https://` URL, typed in, pasted from email or SMS text, read from a QR code, uploaded in bulk, sent through the REST API, or sent from the Chrome extension.
- URL-based machine learning (four models), live website analysis, local threat-intelligence feeds and community reports, combined into one explainable score.
- Investigation and monitoring tools around the scans: history, pivots, a relationship graph, a typosquat finder, a watchlist with alerts, and analytics.
- Running locally on macOS, Linux or Windows, and as a public demo on Vercel (demo mode on a bundled snapshot of demo data).

**Out of scope**

- Scanning email bodies or attachments (the app only *extracts URLs* from pasted text) and analysing downloaded files for malware.
- Running the page's JavaScript in a real browser: pages are fetched with an HTTP client and inspected statically, and the optional screenshot comes from an external service.
- User accounts, API keys and rate limiting: PhishGuard is a single-user project app.
- Taking phishing sites down or reporting them to registrars and hosts.

### How it works

The workflow from the synopsis, as implemented:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["① URL Input<br/>web, email/SMS text, QR,<br/>bulk, API, extension"] --> B["② Validation<br/>scheme, host, port,<br/>normalisation"]
    B --> C["③ Feature Extraction<br/>44 lexical URL features"]
    C --> D["④ Pre-processing<br/>training normalisation,<br/>feature order, scaling"]
    D --> E["⑤ ML Model<br/>4 classifiers,<br/>Random Forest drives"]
    B --> L["Live checks (in parallel)<br/>DNS, WHOIS, SSL, HTTP, content,<br/>brand, feeds, DNSBL, popularity"]
    E --> F["⑥ Risk Classification<br/>60% ML + 40% checks,<br/>blocklist / community floors"]
    L --> F
    F --> G["⑦ Result<br/>verdict, risk 0-100, trust tier,<br/>threat type, explanations"]
```

1. **URL Input.** A URL arrives from the Scan page (single URL, email/SMS text or QR code), a bulk job (up to 500 URLs, scanned 5 at a time in the background), the REST API (`POST /api/scan`) or the Chrome extension. Pasted text can contain several links, including defanged ones such as `hxxp://evil[.]com`, and each one is extracted. The source of every scan (web, text, QR, bulk, API, watchlist or extension) is recorded.
2. **Validation.** The input is trimmed and checked: it must not be empty, contain whitespace or be longer than 4,096 characters. `http://` is added when no scheme is given, only `http` and `https` are accepted, and the URL must have a host with valid labels, a real-looking top-level domain and a valid port. Default ports and the `#fragment` are dropped. Invalid input is rejected with HTTP 422 and a clear message. For the model, the URL is normalised exactly like the training data (trimmed, lower-case, trailing slash removed).
3. **Feature Extraction.** The normalised URL is turned into **44 numeric features**: lengths of the URL, host, path and query, counts of dots, hyphens, `@`, `?`, `=`, digits and special characters, digit ratio, number and length of sub-domains, domain entropy and vowel ratio, IP-address hosts, punycode, ports, `//` redirects, suspicious keywords (`login`, `verify`, `secure`, ...), high-risk TLDs, URL shorteners, free hosting, brand names in the wrong place, brand typosquats, embedded domains, token statistics, path depth, file extensions, percent-encoding and URL entropy. The `https` scheme is deliberately **not** a feature, because most modern phishing sites use HTTPS and the model must not learn "HTTPS means safe".
4. **Pre-processing.** The features are placed in exactly the order used in training. Logistic Regression and the SVM scale them with the `StandardScaler` fitted on the training set (the SVM also uses a Nystroem kernel approximation), and the tree models use the raw values. Training applied the same steps to the dataset after de-duplication, capping each phishing campaign at 3 URLs and a group-aware 80/20 split.
5. **ML Model.** All four trained classifiers score the URL and return a phishing probability. The best model by test F1, **Random Forest**, drives the score, and the others are shown next to it for comparison. The report lists the features that pushed the probability up or down, with their signed impact.

   **Live checks run in parallel with the model.** While the model runs, the analysis engine checks the website itself, using `asyncio` so the slow network lookups overlap instead of running one after another:
   - **SSRF guard:** the host is resolved first, and private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses, or ports other than 80, 443, 8080 and 8443, are refused before any connection is made (checked again on every redirect).
   - **DNS** (A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, SPF/DMARC), then **WHOIS** with an RDAP fallback, the **SSL/TLS certificate**, the **HTTP probe** (redirect chain, headers, forms, scripts, iframes, page content and resources), **DNS blocklists** (Spamhaus DBL and ZEN, SURBL, URIBL, SpamCop) and the optional Google Safe Browsing and VirusTotal lookups all run at the same time, each with its own timeout.
   - **IP geolocation, ASN and hosting**, **brand impersonation** (92 brands), **content category and language**, the **Tranco popularity rank** and a lookup in the **local threat feeds** (about 657,000 entries) complete the picture.

   Each of the 50+ checks gets a status (pass, warn, fail, info or error) and a weight, and together they give a heuristic score from 0 to 100. A failed or timed-out check is reported as an error and never stops the scan. A *quick scan* skips the network checks and uses only the URL features and the model.
6. **Risk Classification.** The two halves are combined as **risk = round(0.6 × ML probability × 100 + 0.4 × heuristic score)**. A hit on a threat-intelligence blocklist raises the risk to at least **90**, and a community report verified by voters raises it to at least **85**. A very popular or official brand domain with no blocklist hit is capped at **30**, but sites on shared hosting platforms such as `vercel.app` never get this cap. The risk then maps to a verdict:

   | Risk score | Verdict | Reputation tier |
   |---|---|---|
   | 0-14 | 🟢 Legitimate | Trusted |
   | 15-34 | 🟢 Legitimate | Favorable |
   | 35-49 | 🟡 Suspicious | Neutral |
   | 50-64 | 🟡 Suspicious | Questionable |
   | 65-100 | 🔴 Phishing | Untrusted |

   The thresholds 35 and 65 can be changed in Settings, and the tiers move with them. The engine also derives a **trust score** (100 − risk) and a **threat type**: social engineering, malware, unwanted software or none.
7. **Result.** The scan is saved in SQLite, written to the activity log, and raises an alert when the risk is high. The user sees the verdict, risk and trust scores, tier, threat type, confidence, a plain-English summary, the positive and negative factors, the score breakdown, and 15 report tabs (Summary, ML Explanation, Domain, Geo & Hosting, SSL, HTTP, Content, Resources, Brand, Reputation, Screenshot, Source, Graph, Timeline and Raw JSON). API clients and the extension get the same result as JSON.

> [!NOTE]
> The synopsis planned a Streamlit page. The final build uses a React dashboard with a FastAPI REST API instead, so the same engine serves the web UI, the Chrome extension, bulk jobs and scripts.

## ✨ Features

**At a glance**

| 🤖 **4** ML models compared | 🔢 **44** URL features | 🧪 **146,364** training URLs | 🏆 Random Forest: **F1 0.856** · **ROC-AUC 0.945** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔍 **50+** live checks in 7 categories | 🏷️ **92** brands watched for impersonation | 🗂️ **16** content categories | 🔤 **13** typosquat techniques |
| 🛑 **5** threat feeds (~**657k** entries) | 📮 **5** DNS blocklist zones | 📑 **15** report tabs | 🖥️ **17** dashboard pages |

### 🤖 Detection & machine learning

- **Four classifiers** (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and SVM) trained on 44 lexical URL features. The best model by test F1, **Random Forest**, drives the score, and all four probabilities are shown side by side in every report.
- **Explainable predictions.** The ML Explanation tab lists the features that pushed the phishing probability up or down, with their signed impact (for example a very long hostname or a brand name in a sub-domain).
- **Hybrid risk score.** 60% ML probability + 40% live-check score, with floors for blocklist hits (≥ 90) and verified community reports (≥ 85), and a cap of 30 for popular or official domains that no engine lists.
- **Three verdicts and a full risk picture:** Legitimate / Suspicious / Phishing, a 0-100 risk score, a trust score (100 − risk), five reputation tiers (Trusted → Untrusted), a threat type (social engineering, malware, unwanted software) and a confidence value.
- **Plain-English summary** plus separate **negative and positive factor** lists, so every verdict can be traced back to its causes.
- **Model Lab page** with the dataset composition, the model comparison table, ROC and precision-recall curves, confusion matrices, feature importance, per-class feature averages, the "with / without scheme" comparison and a realistic held-out test on 4,000 URLs from unseen domains.
- **Adjustable thresholds.** The suspicious (35) and phishing (65) cut-offs can be changed in Settings, and tiers and verdicts follow them.

### 🔍 Deep URL analysis

- **50+ checks in 7 categories** (URL/lexical, domain, network, SSL/TLS, HTTP and page content, brand, reputation). Each check has a status (pass, warn, fail, info or error) and a weight, and the slow network checks run in parallel.
- **8-stage deep scan** with live progress: lexical analysis, ML prediction, DNS, WHOIS, SSL/TLS, HTTP and content, brand impersonation, reputation. A quick scan (URL features and model only) is one click away.
- **Domain:** WHOIS registrar, creation and expiry dates and privacy, with an **RDAP fallback** when the `whois` command is missing (as on Vercel). DNS A, AAAA, MX, NS and TXT records with SPF and DMARC checks.
- **Geo & hosting:** IP geolocation, ASN and hosting provider (ip-api.com, with ipwho.is as fallback).
- **SSL/TLS:** issuer, validity window, days left, certificate age, SANs, protocol, hostname mismatch and self-signed detection.
- **HTTP probe:** redirect chain, status, response time, server, security headers, technologies, forms (password fields, forms posting to another domain), links, iframes, external scripts, meta refresh and suspicious JavaScript patterns.
- **Brand impersonation** for 92 brands through typosquatting, homoglyphs, combosquatting, brand-as-sub-domain, punycode, path and page-content techniques.
- **Content:** page category (16 classes such as banking, payment, login, crypto and parked), page language with a one-click translate link, parked-domain detection and tracker IDs (Google Analytics, GTM, Facebook Pixel, AdSense, Hotjar).
- **Resources & source:** every script, stylesheet, image, frame and form the page references, the contacted domains (first or third party), and the stored HTML of the final page (gzipped, up to 500 KB) with line numbers and search.
- **Screenshot tab:** an optional page screenshot from the thum.io service (off by default, turned on in Settings).
- **SSRF guard:** before connecting to a scanned site, every resolved address must be public, and this is checked again on every redirect. Private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses are refused, and only ports 80, 443, 8080 and 8443 are allowed.

### 🛑 Threat intelligence

- **Local threat feeds:** OpenPhish, PhishTank, URLhaus, Phishing.Database and Phishing Army, about **657,000 entries** in the current snapshot, with search, top targeted brands and top TLDs on the Threat Feeds page.
- **Multi-engine verdict:** every feed, five DNS blocklist zones (Spamhaus DBL and ZEN, SURBL, URIBL, SpamCop) and the PhishGuard ML engine count as engines, and the report shows **"N of M engines flagged"** with a per-engine table.
- **Optional Google Safe Browsing and VirusTotal lookups** when you add your own API keys in Settings.
- **Tranco popularity rank**, used as a strong "safe" signal for well-known sites (never for shared hosting platforms such as `vercel.app` or URL shorteners).
- **Typosquat finder:** dnstwist-style permutations of a domain with 13 techniques (omission, insertion, repetition, transposition, replacement, homoglyph, bitsquatting, vowel swap, hyphenation, addition, sub-domain, TLD swap and dictionary), checked live in DNS to show which look-alikes actually resolve.

### 🔔 Monitoring & alerts

- **Watchlist:** re-check URLs or domains on a schedule (every 15 minutes to weekly in the dashboard, 1 minute to 7 days through the API), optionally watch for newly resolving look-alike domains, and see each item's check history. On the Vercel demo the checks run once a day through Vercel Cron.
- **Alerts** for high-risk scans, verdict changes on watched items, new resolving typosquats, bulk jobs that found phishing and community verification, with an unread counter in the header bell.
- **Activity log:** an audit trail of scans, rescans, deletions, reports, votes, bulk jobs, watchlist and settings changes, feed refreshes and exports. Each event is linked to its scan or domain and feeds the report's **Timeline** tab.

### 👥 Community reporting

- **PhishTank-style reports:** anyone can report a URL as phishing or legitimate, and others vote on it. The reporter's label counts as the first vote.
- A report is **verified** at a net **+3** phishing votes and **rejected** at **−3**. A verified report raises the URL's risk to at least 85, and its status shows up in the report's Reputation tab.

### 📊 Analytics & tracking

- **Overview dashboard:** KPIs (total scans, detection rate, average trust score and more), scans over time, the verdict split, a risk-score histogram, top impersonated brands, top hosting countries, recent alerts, model health and a **live scan feed** that refreshes every 5 seconds.
- **Analytics page** for 24 h, 7 d, 30 d, 90 d or all time: scans and average risk over time, a weekday × hour heatmap, TLDs, scan sources, impersonation techniques, SSL status, domain age, top failing checks, countries, top domains, threat types, reputation tiers, content categories, a **detection funnel** (scanned → reachable → login form → brand impersonation → feed listed → phishing verdict), throughput and check error rates.
- **History:** search, filters, sorting and **CSV / JSON export** (CSV cells are protected against spreadsheet formula injection).
- **Domain page** with every scan of a domain and its risk trend.

### 🕸️ Investigation (graph, pivots)

- **Relationship graph** (Graph page and the report's Graph tab): scanned domains linked through shared IP addresses, ASNs, name servers, registrars, countries, impersonated brands and redirects, drawn as an interactive force-directed graph.
- **One-click pivots:** IP, ASN, registrar, content category, threat type and tier values in a report are links that open History filtered on that value (for example *all Untrusted sites* or *everything on this IP*).
- **Similar scans** on the same IP, ASN or registrar, listed in each report.
- **Compare** any two scans of the same domain side by side, and **rescan** a URL to see how it changed.
- **Timeline** of everything that happened to a scan or domain (scanned, rescanned, reported, voted, watched).

### 🔌 REST API & Chrome extension

- **Documented REST API** under `/api` (JSON, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps) with interactive **Swagger UI at [`/docs`](https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/docs)** and ReDoc at `/redoc`. The in-app **API Guide** page has copy-paste `curl` examples grouped by task.
- **Bulk scanning** of up to 500 URLs per job (JSON list or CSV/TXT upload), processed in the background 5 at a time, with live progress.
- **URL extraction** from email or SMS text, including defanged links such as `hxxp://evil[.]com`. QR codes are decoded right in the browser.
- **Chrome extension** (Manifest V3, plain JavaScript, no build step): scans the current tab, shows the risk score as a coloured toolbar badge, warns with a desktop notification and an optional in-page banner, and adds a **"Scan link with PhishGuard"** item to the right-click menu. See [`extension/README.md`](extension/README.md).

### Feature parity with popular tools

PhishGuard's feature set comes from researching 12 public URL-safety services ([`docs/FEATURES.md`](docs/FEATURES.md)). The matrix lists **only features PhishGuard actually has**, and marks which of the 12 tools offer each one as a user-facing feature (based on that research, Oct 2026). No single tool covers more than 21 of these 38 features. PhishGuard brings all of them together in one free, open-source app.

## 📸 Screenshots

Every page of the dashboard, every tab of a scan report, dark mode and the phone layout, captured from the running app with demo data; each image has a short note on what it shows and why it matters.

<!-- gallery generated by scripts/build_readme.py from docs/media/screenshots.json -->

**49 screenshots** in 11 groups: Dashboard (1) · Scanning (4) · Scan report (14) · History & bulk (3) · Analytics (5) · Machine learning (5) · Investigation (3) · Monitoring (3) · Community & intel (2) · Tracking & settings (4) · Responsive & themes (5)

### Dashboard

**1. Overview dashboard**

The landing page summarises detection activity for the selected time range: total, phishing and legitimate scans, detection rate, average trust and risk scores, blacklist hits and impersonated brands. Charts of scans over time, the verdict split, the risk-score distribution, top impersonated brands and hosting countries sit next to a live scan feed, model health and recent alerts, so the current phishing picture is visible at a glance.

<img src="docs/media/01-overview.png" alt="Overview dashboard" width="100%">

### Scanning

**2. Scan a single URL**

The Scan page takes one URL and runs the full analysis pipeline. The Deep scan toggle adds live DNS, WHOIS, SSL, HTTP and page-content checks on top of the instant lexical and ML analysis, and the example links let a reviewer try a legitimate site, a typosquatted PayPal URL and a raw-IP banking page in one click.

<img src="docs/media/02-scan-url.png" alt="Scan a single URL" width="100%">

**3. Extract URLs from an email or SMS**

A suspicious email or SMS is pasted as text and PhishGuard extracts every link in it, including defanged forms such as hxxp:// and [.]. The extracted URLs can be ticked and scanned in one go, which matches how phishing really arrives: inside messages rather than as bare links.

<img src="docs/media/03-scan-email-sms.png" alt="Extract URLs from an email or SMS" width="100%">

**4. Scan a QR code (quishing)**

A QR-code image is decoded locally in the browser with jsQR, so the image is never uploaded, and the embedded URL is shown before anything is opened. One click then scans the decoded link, which protects against QR-code phishing on posters, invoices and parcel notices.

<img src="docs/media/04-scan-qr.png" alt="Scan a QR code (quishing)" width="100%">

**5. Scan in progress**

While a deep scan runs, the analysis-pipeline card ticks off each stage: lexical analysis, ML prediction, DNS, WHOIS, SSL/TLS, HTTP and content, brand impersonation and reputation. It makes the multi-signal design visible and tells the user what is being checked before the report opens.

<img src="docs/media/05-scan-progress.png" alt="Scan in progress" width="100%">

### Scan report

**6. Report: summary, AI summary and factors**

The report header shows the 0-100 risk gauge, verdict, trust score and tier, threat type, engines flagged, ML probability and scan duration for a live phishing kit hosted on vercel.app. The Summary tab adds a plain-English AI summary, the negative and positive factors behind the score, the score breakdown (60% ML + 40% heuristics) and every security check, so the verdict can be explained instead of being a black box.

<img src="docs/media/06-report-summary.png" alt="Report: summary, AI summary and factors" width="100%">

**7. Report: ML explanation**

The ML Explanation tab shows the primary model (Random Forest), its phishing probability and how many of the four classifiers agree. Signed feature contributions show which URL properties pushed the prediction towards phishing or safe, and the table lists every lexical feature extracted from the URL.

<img src="docs/media/07-report-ml-explanation.png" alt="Report: ML explanation" width="100%">

**8. Report: domain and WHOIS**

The Domain tab splits the hostname into subdomain, registered domain and TLD and shows WHOIS data (registrar, created, updated and expiry dates) and DNS records. Domain age is a strong phishing signal; here the registered domain is old because the kit sits on a free hosting platform, which the subdomain and hosting checks expose.

<img src="docs/media/08-report-domain-whois.png" alt="Report: domain and WHOIS" width="100%">

**9. Report: geo and hosting**

Geo & Hosting resolves the server IP to its country, city, ASN, organisation and ISP, flags hosting/datacenter networks and pins the location on an OpenStreetMap map. This helps to spot phishing pages on cheap hosting and to group sites that share infrastructure.

<img src="docs/media/09-report-geo-hosting.png" alt="Report: geo and hosting" width="100%">

**10. Report: SSL certificate**

The SSL tab shows the certificate issuer, subject, protocol, validity window, days left and SANs, and explains why validation failed (here a hostname mismatch). Free, short-lived or mismatched certificates are common on phishing sites, so the certificate feeds into the heuristic score.

<img src="docs/media/10-report-ssl.png" alt="Report: SSL certificate" width="100%">

**11. Report: HTTP analysis**

The HTTP tab follows the redirect chain hop by hop, shows the response details and which of six security headers are present, and detects technologies and suspicious JavaScript (obfuscated eval, exfiltration to a Telegram bot, visitor geo-lookup). The page-content counters (forms, password fields, external scripts) reveal a credential-harvesting login form.

<img src="docs/media/11-report-http.png" alt="Report: HTTP analysis" width="100%">

**12. Report: brand impersonation**

For a scan that impersonates MetaMask, the Brand tab names the targeted brand, the technique (the brand used as a subdomain of an unrelated vercel.app domain) and the similarity to the genuine brand domain. The table explains the tricks attackers use to look legitimate: typosquats, homoglyphs, combosquats, punycode, brand in the path or in the page content.

<img src="docs/media/12-report-brand.png" alt="Report: brand impersonation" width="100%">

**13. Report: reputation and detection engines**

The Reputation tab lists every detection engine with its type and result: five local threat feeds (OpenPhish, URLhaus, Phishing.Database, PhishTank, Phishing Army), five DNS blocklists and the PhishGuard ML engine. It also shows which blacklists contain the URL and the community verdict with its votes, so the ML score is cross-checked against independent sources.

<img src="docs/media/13-report-reputation.png" alt="Report: reputation and detection engines" width="100%">

**14. Report: page content**

The Content tab classifies the live page (here a login page with 95% confidence), detects its language and checks whether the domain is parked. Category scores and the tracker list explain what the page is trying to do, for example harvesting webmail credentials.

<img src="docs/media/14-report-content.png" alt="Report: page content" width="100%">

**15. Report: resources**

The Resources tab counts every script, style, image, frame and form the page loads and the domains it contacts. A login page that pulls all of its resources from third-party domains is typical of a copied phishing kit.

<img src="docs/media/15-report-resources.png" alt="Report: resources" width="100%">

**16. Report: page source**

The Source tab shows the stored HTML as plain text with line numbers, search, wrapping and copy; the page is never rendered. The phishing kit's markup and scripts can be inspected safely without visiting the live site.

<img src="docs/media/16-report-source.png" alt="Report: page source" width="100%">

**17. Report: relationship graph**

The Graph tab draws the infrastructure around the scanned domain up to two hops: its URL, IP address, ASN, name servers, registrar, country and the other scanned domains that share them. Shared infrastructure links a single phishing site to related campaigns.

<img src="docs/media/17-report-graph.png" alt="Report: relationship graph" width="100%">

**18. Report: timeline**

The Timeline tab lists the events recorded for this scan and its domain (scans, community reports, watchlist runs and alerts), each with expandable details. It shows how a phishing site was detected, reported and monitored over time.

<img src="docs/media/18-report-timeline.png" alt="Report: timeline" width="100%">

**19. Report: legitimate (Trusted) site**

For https://github.com the gauge shows risk 3/100, tier Trusted, 0 of 11 engines flagged and a 4.3% ML phishing probability. The AI summary and the positive factors (official domain, valid certificate, not on any feed) show that safe verdicts are explained as clearly as phishing ones, which keeps false positives understandable.

<img src="docs/media/19-report-legitimate.png" alt="Report: legitimate (Trusted) site" width="100%">

### History & bulk

**20. History with pivot filters**

Scan history combines search, verdict, source, TLD, risk-range and date filters with advanced pivots (IP, ASN, registrar, content category, threat type, trust tier). Active filters appear as removable chips and are kept in the URL, so a view such as 'all untrusted social-engineering scans' can be shared or exported to CSV/JSON.

<img src="docs/media/20-history-pivot-filters.png" alt="History with pivot filters" width="100%">

**21. Bulk scan**

Up to 500 URLs are pasted or uploaded as a CSV/TXT file; duplicates are removed and the job runs in the background. The jobs table tracks the progress and verdict split of every job.

<img src="docs/media/21-bulk-scan.png" alt="Bulk scan" width="100%">

**22. Bulk job results**

A finished bulk job shows its progress, the verdict distribution and every URL with its verdict, risk score, impersonated brand, blacklist status and scan time, with CSV/JSON export. A list of reported links can be triaged in one pass, and phishing URLs that are on no blacklist yet are still caught by the model.

<img src="docs/media/22-bulk-job-detail.png" alt="Bulk job results" width="100%">

### Analytics

**23. Analytics: trends and activity heatmap**

Scans over time are stacked by verdict next to the average risk trend, and the heatmap shows scan activity by weekday and hour (UTC). Together they show when phishing activity peaks and whether risk is rising.

<img src="docs/media/23-analytics-trends.png" alt="Analytics: trends and activity heatmap" width="100%">

**24. Analytics: distributions**

Charts break the scans down by top-level domain, scan source (web, bulk, extension, API, watch, text, QR), impersonation technique, SSL status, domain age and the checks that fail most often. They show which signals separate phishing from legitimate sites in the collected data.

<img src="docs/media/24-analytics-distributions.png" alt="Analytics: distributions" width="100%">

**25. Analytics: threat insights**

Threat types (Safe Browsing-style), reputation tiers and content categories summarise what kind of threats were found. Clicking a slice or bar opens the matching scans in History.

<img src="docs/media/25-analytics-threat-insights.png" alt="Analytics: threat insights" width="100%">

**26. Analytics: detection funnel**

The funnel shows how many scans pass each detection stage: scanned, reachable, login/password form, brand impersonation, listed in a feed and phishing verdict. It shows how the individual signals narrow down to the final phishing verdicts.

<img src="docs/media/26-analytics-funnel.png" alt="Analytics: detection funnel" width="100%">

**27. Analytics: performance**

P50, P95, P99 and maximum scan latency, the error count, hourly throughput and per-check error rates measure how fast and reliable the analysis engine is. The median deep scan, with all network checks, finishes in under two seconds.

<img src="docs/media/27-analytics-performance.png" alt="Analytics: performance" width="100%">

### Machine learning

**28. Model Lab: dataset and model comparison**

The Model Lab shows the training dataset (146,364 URLs from PhiUSIIL, PhishTank, Phishing.Database, OpenPhish and Tranco, balanced 50/50), live prediction statistics and a comparison of Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and SVM on accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, 5-fold cross-validation and timing. Random Forest has the best F1 (85.6%) and ROC-AUC (0.945) and is used for scoring.

<img src="docs/media/28-model-lab-comparison.png" alt="Model Lab: dataset and model comparison" width="100%">

**29. Model Lab: realistic evaluation**

Besides the stratified test split, every model is evaluated on 4,000 held-out URLs from campaigns and domains never seen in training (PhishTank and Phishing.Database phishing, Tranco deep links). F1, precision, recall, HTTPS recall and false-positive rate on this set give an honest estimate of real-world accuracy, and the composition card shows where the training URLs came from.

<img src="docs/media/29-model-lab-realistic-evaluation.png" alt="Model Lab: realistic evaluation" width="100%">

**30. Model Lab: ROC and precision-recall curves**

ROC and precision-recall curves of the four classifiers on the test split, with the best model drawn thicker. They show the trade-off between catching phishing and raising false alarms at every threshold.

<img src="docs/media/30-model-lab-roc-pr.png" alt="Model Lab: ROC and precision-recall curves" width="100%">

**31. Model Lab: confusion matrices**

One confusion matrix per model counts true/false positives and negatives on the 29,272-URL test split. Missed phishing (false negatives) and blocked legitimate sites (false positives) are the two errors that matter in practice.

<img src="docs/media/31-model-lab-confusion-matrices.png" alt="Model Lab: confusion matrices" width="100%">

**32. Model Lab: feature importance**

The top 20 Random Forest features and the mean of each feature in phishing vs legitimate samples explain what the model learned. Subdomain length, free-hosting platforms and hostname length matter most, and phishing hostnames are much longer on average (25.3 vs 16.5 characters).

<img src="docs/media/32-model-lab-feature-importance.png" alt="Model Lab: feature importance" width="100%">

### Investigation

**33. Domain intelligence**

The Domain page aggregates every scan of one domain: scan count, average risk, latest verdict, first and last seen, a risk trend and the latest IP, hosting, registrar, domain age and SSL issuer. From here the domain can be watched, re-scanned or checked for typosquats.

<img src="docs/media/33-domain-intelligence.png" alt="Domain intelligence" width="100%">

**34. Relationship graph with a node selected**

The Graph page links scanned domains through shared IPs, ASNs, name servers, registrars, brands and redirects, here centred on a MetaMask phishing domain at depth 2. Selecting the domain highlights its neighbours and opens a side panel with its verdict, risk, connections and pivots, which helps to uncover campaigns that reuse the same infrastructure.

<img src="docs/media/34-graph-node-selected.png" alt="Relationship graph with a node selected" width="100%">

**35. Typosquat finder (paypal.com)**

dnstwist-style permutations of paypal.com (omission, transposition, homoglyph, TLD swap, dictionary words and more, 13 techniques) are generated and checked in DNS. Here 50 of the 60 checked lookalikes resolve, each with its IP and a one-click scan, which shows how many domains could be used to impersonate a single brand.

<img src="docs/media/35-typosquat-paypal.png" alt="Typosquat finder (paypal.com)" width="100%">

### Monitoring

**36. Watchlist**

URLs and domains are re-checked automatically on an interval; each target shows its last verdict, risk, change and alert count, and brand domains can also be monitored for newly resolving typosquats. A verdict change or a new lookalike raises an alert.

<img src="docs/media/36-watchlist.png" alt="Watchlist" width="100%">

**37. Watchlist history**

The history drawer of a monitored target charts its risk over time against the suspicious (35) and phishing (65) thresholds and lists every check with a link to its report. For a brand domain such as paypal.com it also lists the resolving typosquats, the lookalikes most likely to be used against that brand.

<img src="docs/media/37-watchlist-history.png" alt="Watchlist history" width="100%">

**38. Alerts**

Alerts are raised by high-risk scans, watchlist changes, typosquat baselines and community verification, with severity filters and read/unread state. Each alert links to the scan or watchlist entry that caused it.

<img src="docs/media/38-alerts.png" alt="Alerts" width="100%">

### Community & intel

**39. Community reports**

Anyone can report a suspicious URL with a label, targeted brand and comment; reports are verified PhishTank-style at +3 net phishing votes and rejected at -3. The Pending, Verified and Rejected tabs show the reporter, status and votes, and a verified report raises the risk score of that URL.

<img src="docs/media/39-community.png" alt="Community reports" width="100%">

**40. Threat feeds**

PhishGuard keeps local copies of five public blocklists (OpenPhish, URLhaus, Phishing.Database, PhishTank and Phishing Army, about 657,000 entries) that can be refreshed on demand. Charts show the entries per feed, top TLDs and most targeted brands, and any URL, domain or brand can be searched across all feeds.

<img src="docs/media/40-threat-feeds.png" alt="Threat feeds" width="100%">

### Tracking & settings

**41. Activity log**

The activity log is an audit trail of scans, alerts, watchlist runs, community reports, votes, bulk jobs, typosquat searches and settings changes, filterable by event type and with expandable details. It makes every action of the system traceable.

<img src="docs/media/41-activity-log.png" alt="Activity log" width="100%">

**42. Settings**

Verdict thresholds (35 suspicious, 65 phishing) are set with sliders and a live preview; other options switch network checks and page screenshots, set the check timeout and data retention and store optional VirusTotal / Google Safe Browsing keys. The About section names the project, student, guide and institute and shows the seven-step system workflow.

<img src="docs/media/42-settings.png" alt="Settings" width="100%">

**43. API guide**

The API guide lists the REST endpoints with copy-paste curl examples for scanning, history, export, bulk jobs, URL extraction, typosquats, community reports and the watchlist. Any tool or script can use the same engine as the dashboard, for example to check links from a mail gateway.

<img src="docs/media/43-api-guide.png" alt="API guide" width="100%">

**44. Swagger / OpenAPI docs**

FastAPI serves interactive OpenAPI documentation at /docs, where every endpoint can be tried from the browser. The description documents the scoring formula: risk = 0.6 x ML probability x 100 + 0.4 x heuristic score, raised on a blacklist hit or a verified community report.

<img src="docs/media/44-swagger-docs.png" alt="Swagger / OpenAPI docs" width="100%">

## 🏗️ Architecture

PhishGuard is a three-tier web application: two browser clients (the **React dashboard** and a **Chrome extension**), one **FastAPI REST API** with a shared scan pipeline (**ML predictor** + **analysis engine** + **risk scoring**), and a single **SQLite** database. The same code runs locally (Uvicorn + Vite) and on Vercel (one Python serverless function in demo mode plus the static frontend).

The seven diagrams below were drawn from the source code, and the file and function names in their labels point to the code behind each step. GitHub renders the Mermaid blocks inline; a static PNG of each diagram is linked underneath for viewers without Mermaid support.

| # | Diagram | What it answers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [High-level system architecture](#1-high-level-system-architecture) | Which parts exist and how they talk to each other |
| 2 | [Scan pipeline](#2-scan-pipeline-post-apiscan) | What happens, step by step, when a URL is scanned |
| 3 | [ML training and inference pipeline](#3-ml-training-and-inference-pipeline) | How the dataset is built, the models trained and the best one used at scan time |
| 4 | [Risk scoring decision flow](#4-risk-scoring-decision-flow) | How the ML probability, the checks, the feeds and community votes become one score |
| 5 | [Database ER diagram](#5-database-er-diagram) | The 11 SQLite tables and their relations |
| 6 | [Deployment: local vs Vercel](#6-deployment-local-vs-vercel) | How the local run and the hosted demo differ |
| 7 | [Frontend route map](#7-frontend-route-map) | Every dashboard page and the API endpoints it calls |

### 1. High-level system architecture

PhishGuard is a three-tier web application. There are two browser clients: the React dashboard and a Manifest V3
Chrome extension. Both call one FastAPI REST API (48 endpoints in 14 routers). Every scan goes through the same
`perform_scan()` pipeline, whether it comes from the dashboard, the extension, a bulk job, the watchlist scheduler
or a community report. That pipeline runs the ML predictor and the analysis engine side by side. Only the engine
talks to the internet. Live probes of the scanned site (HTTP and TLS) go through the SSRF guard, while DNS,
WHOIS/RDAP, DNSBL and geo-IP are third-party lookups. Threat feeds and the Tranco list are local files, and all
state is kept in one SQLite database.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph clients["Clients (browser)"]
        uiDash["React dashboard<br/>Vite SPA, 19 routes"]
        uiExt["Chrome extension<br/>Manifest V3: popup,<br/>context menu, banner"]
    end

    subgraph apiLayer["REST API"]
        apiRouters["FastAPI app.main<br/>14 routers, 48 endpoints<br/>Swagger UI at /docs"]
    end

    subgraph services["Services"]
        direction LR
        svcBulk["Bulk jobs<br/>max 500 URLs,<br/>5 at a time"]
        svcWatch["Watcher<br/>60 s scheduler<br/>+ retention"]
        svcCommunity["Community<br/>reports + votes"]
        svcAnalytics["Analytics, graph,<br/>similar scans"]
        svcScanner["Scanner<br/>perform_scan()"]
        svcEvents["Events + alerts"]
        svcBulk --> svcScanner
        svcWatch --> svcScanner
        svcCommunity --> svcScanner
        svcScanner --> svcEvents
    end

    subgraph core["Detection core"]
        mlPredictor["ML predictor<br/>4 models,<br/>Random Forest decides"]
        engine["Analysis engine<br/>run_checks(),<br/>about 60 checks"]
        guard["SSRF guard<br/>net_safety.py"]
    end

    subgraph localData["Local data files"]
        direction LR
        artifacts["Model artifacts<br/>4 x .joblib + metrics.json"]
        feeds["Threat feeds: OpenPhish,<br/>PhishTank, URLhaus,<br/>Phishing.Database,<br/>Phishing Army"]
        tranco["Tranco top-1M index"]
    end

    subgraph internet["Third-party lookups"]
        direction LR
        extDns["DNS resolvers"]
        extWhois["WHOIS / RDAP"]
        extDnsbl["DNSBL: Spamhaus,<br/>SURBL, URIBL, SpamCop"]
        extGeo["Geo-IP: ip-api.com,<br/>ipwho.is"]
        extOptional["Optional: Google Safe<br/>Browsing, VirusTotal"]
    end

    extTarget["Scanned website<br/>HTTP pages +<br/>TLS certificate"]
    db[("SQLite, WAL mode<br/>backend/data/<br/>phishguard.db")]

    clients -->|"JSON over HTTP"| apiLayer
    apiLayer --> services
    services -->|"read / write"| db
    svcScanner -->|"in parallel"| mlPredictor
    svcScanner -->|"in parallel"| engine
    mlPredictor --> artifacts
    engine --> feeds
    engine --> tranco
    engine --> internet
    engine --> guard
    guard -->|"live probes"| extTarget
```

### 2. Scan pipeline (`POST /api/scan`)

`perform_scan()` in `services/scanner.py` first checks and normalises the URL. Then it runs three tasks at the same
time with `asyncio.gather`: the ML prediction (in a thread), the analysis engine, and a threat-feed lookup on the
API side. Inside the engine the SSRF guard runs first. If the host resolves to a private address or uses a port
that is not allowed, the TLS and HTTP probes are skipped and a `private_network_host` check is added. The scores
are combined in `app/scoring.py`. The result is stored as indexed columns plus the full JSON document, and an event
(and sometimes a critical alert) is written before the `ScanResult` is returned. With `deep=false`, or with network
checks turned off in Settings, only the URL-based checks and the ML model run, and the result is marked
`tested_depth = lexical`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client<br/>(dashboard / extension)
    participant R as API router<br/>routers/scans.py
    participant S as Scanner<br/>services/scanner.py
    participant M as ML predictor<br/>ml/predictor.py
    participant E as Analysis engine<br/>analysis/engine.py
    participant N as Network<br/>(DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, TLS,<br/>HTTP, DNSBL, geo-IP)
    participant K as Scoring<br/>app/scoring.py
    participant D as SQLite

    C->>R: POST /api/scan {url, deep, source}
    R->>S: perform_scan(url, source, deep)
    Note over S: normalize_url(): add http:// if missing,<br/>http/https only, valid host and TLD,<br/>otherwise HTTP 422
    S->>D: get_settings(): thresholds, timeout, toggles
    par ML model (worker thread)
        S->>M: predict(normalized_url)
        Note over M: 44 lexical features,<br/>4 model probabilities,<br/>perturbation explanations
        M-->>S: probability_phishing, per_model, explanations
    and Analysis engine (budget max(25 s, 2 × timeout + 10 s))
        S->>E: run_checks(url, engine_settings)
        E->>N: SSRF guard: resolve host, every IP must be public,<br/>port 80, 443, 8080 or 8443
        par network probes (asyncio.gather)
            E->>N: DNS A/AAAA/MX/NS/TXT, then geo-IP + IP DNSBL
            E->>N: WHOIS, with RDAP fallback
            E->>N: TLS handshake on port 443
            E->>N: HTTP probe, every redirect hop re-checked
            E->>N: domain DNSBL, optional Safe Browsing / VirusTotal
        end
        Note over E: local feeds + Tranco rank,<br/>brand detection, content analysis<br/>(category, language, parked)
        Note over E: build_checks() + score_checks()<br/>= heuristic score 0-100
        E-->>S: checks, domain_info, ssl, http, brand,<br/>reputation, heuristic_score, dom_html
    and Threat-feed lookup (worker thread)
        Note over S: feeds.lookup(normalized_url)<br/>against the local feed sets
    end
    S->>D: community_for(domain, url) from reports
    S->>K: compute_score(ml_prob, heuristic, blacklisted, community_verified)
    K-->>S: risk = round(0.6 × ML × 100 + 0.4 × heuristic),<br/>floors 90 / 85, verdict, confidence
    S->>K: finalize(result, settings)
    K-->>S: popular/official cap 30, trust score, tier,<br/>threat type, factors, summary
    S->>D: INSERT scans (columns + JSON), scan_dom (gzipped HTML)
    S->>D: log_event("scan") into events
    opt verdict is phishing and (risk ≥ 80 or blacklisted), and no alert for this domain in the last hour
        S->>D: create_alert("high_risk_scan", critical)
    end
    S-->>R: ScanResult
    R-->>C: 200 OK with the ScanResult JSON
```

### 3. ML training and inference pipeline

Training (`python -m ml.train`, about 100 s) reads only local snapshots under `backend/ml/data/raw/`. After
deduplication and bias fixes, the dataset has 146,364 URLs. It is split by *campaign key* (registered domain, or the
tenant host on free-hosting platforms), so no campaign appears in both train and test. All four models are trained
twice, with and without the `uses_https` feature. The scheme-free variant (44 features) was kept because it is more
robust on a held-out "modern" set of 4,000 URLs. Random Forest has the best test F1 and makes the decision. The other
three models are still shown on every scan report.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph sources["Data sources: snapshots in backend/ml/data/raw"]
        srcPhiusiil["PhiUSIIL, UCI dataset 967<br/>45,000 phishing<br/>40,753 legit"]
        srcPhishtank["PhishTank<br/>verified-online<br/>16,000 phishing"]
        srcPhishdb["Phishing.Database<br/>ACTIVE list<br/>12,000 phishing"]
        srcOpenphish["OpenPhish feed<br/>241 phishing"]
        srcTranco["Tranco top-30k<br/>21,825 legit domains<br/>6,448 legit sub-domains"]
        srcSitemaps["Sitemaps of<br/>Tranco sites<br/>4,097 legit deep links"]
    end

    subgraph prep["Cleaning and bias mitigation"]
        direction LR
        prepClean["Normalise: lower-case,<br/>no trailing slash<br/>Dedupe across sources<br/>Max 3 URLs per campaign"]
        prepAugment["Legit hosts augmented:<br/>www toggled, about 40%<br/>get deep-link paths<br/>Host-only feeds get an<br/>imputed scheme and path"]
        prepDataset["Dataset: 146,364 URLs<br/>73,241 phishing<br/>73,123 legitimate"]
        prepClean --> prepAugment --> prepDataset
    end

    featExtract["extract_features() in ml/features.py<br/>45 lexical URL features<br/>scheme-free variant keeps 44"]
    split["StratifiedGroupKFold 80/20<br/>grouped by campaign key<br/>train 117,092 / test 29,272"]

    subgraph models["Four scikit-learn classifiers"]
        mLr["Logistic Regression<br/>test F1 0.8045"]
        mDt["Decision Tree<br/>depth 20<br/>test F1 0.8372"]
        mRf["Random Forest<br/>150 trees<br/>test F1 0.8561<br/>ROC-AUC 0.9449"]
        mSvm["SVM: Nystroem RBF<br/>+ LinearSVC, calibrated<br/>test F1 0.8329"]
    end

    evalTest["Test metrics: accuracy, precision,<br/>recall, F1, ROC-AUC, confusion matrix,<br/>ROC and PR curves, 5-fold group CV<br/>(RF CV F1 0.855 ± 0.002)"]
    evalModern["Held-out modern set, 4,000 URLs:<br/>PhishTank + Phishing.Database +<br/>Tranco ranks 30k-60k deep links<br/>picks the feature variant"]
    best["Best test F1: Random Forest<br/>saved to backend/ml/artifacts:<br/>4 x .joblib + metrics.json<br/>version 2026.10.24-1812"]

    subgraph infer["Inference at scan time: ml/predictor.py"]
        direction LR
        inferPredict["predict(url): artifacts loaded<br/>once, lazy and thread-safe<br/>44 features, 4 probabilities<br/>Random Forest value is used"]
        inferExplain["Explanations: each differing<br/>feature reset to the legit median<br/>change in probability = impact<br/>top 10 returned"]
        inferPredict --> inferExplain
    end

    sources --> prep
    prep --> featExtract --> split --> models
    models --> evalTest
    models --> evalModern
    evalTest --> best
    evalModern -.->|"variant choice"| best
    best --> infer
```

### 4. Risk scoring decision flow

The final risk score combines the ML probability (60%) with the engine's heuristic score (40%). A hit on any
blocklist raises the score to at least 90, and a verified community report raises it to at least 85. `finalize()`
then caps the score at 30 for popular or official domains, but only when nothing lists them and there is no malware
evidence. It also derives the trust score, the reputation tier and the threat type, with malware taking precedence
over social engineering and unwanted software. Confidence (not drawn) is the distance from the nearest threshold,
and it is at least 0.9 when a blocklist or verified report decided the score. Note: the popularity cap checks the
`popular_site` check, which passes for any domain that has a Tranco rank. So in practice it applies to every Tranco
top-1M domain, not only the top 10k mentioned in the code's docstring.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph stHeur["Heuristic score h: engine.py"]
        direction TB
        hRaw["raw = sum of failed-check weights<br/>+ 0.4 × sum of warning weights"]
        hCurve["h = 100 × (1 − e^(−raw / 18))"]
        hFloors["Raise h to a floor:<br/>blacklisted 92<br/>brand + login form 85<br/>password sent off-site 80<br/>brand impersonation 75<br/>malicious JavaScript 60<br/>raw IP host 55<br/>domain under 30 days 55<br/>bad redirects 50, punycode 50<br/>invalid SSL 45, risky TLD 35"]
        hCaps["Then cap h:<br/>official brand domain 15<br/>Tranco top 10k with<br/>no hard fail 20"]
        hRaw --> hCurve --> hFloors --> hCaps
    end

    subgraph stScore["Risk score and verdict: scoring.py"]
        direction TB
        base["risk = round(0.6 × p × 100 + 0.4 × h)<br/>p = ML phishing probability"]
        qBlacklist{"Blacklisted?"}
        fBlacklist["risk = max(risk, 90)"]
        qCommunity{"Verified<br/>community<br/>report?"}
        fCommunity["risk = max(risk, 85)"]
        verdict["Verdict, default thresholds:<br/>65-100 phishing<br/>35-64 suspicious<br/>0-34 legitimate"]
        base --> qBlacklist
        qBlacklist -->|"yes"| fBlacklist --> qCommunity
        qBlacklist -->|"no"| qCommunity
        qCommunity -->|"yes"| fCommunity --> verdict
        qCommunity -->|"no"| verdict
    end

    subgraph stCap["Cap and tier: finalize()"]
        direction TB
        qHard{"Any listing,<br/>verified report or<br/>malware evidence?"}
        qPopular{"Official brand<br/>domain or Tranco-<br/>ranked, not a<br/>hosting platform?"}
        fCap["Risk above 30 is<br/>capped at 30,<br/>verdict re-derived"]
        trust["trust_score = 100 − risk"]
        tier["Tier:<br/>0-14 Trusted<br/>15-34 Favorable<br/>35-49 Neutral<br/>50-64 Questionable<br/>65-100 Untrusted"]
        qHard -->|"yes: no cap"| trust
        qHard -->|"no"| qPopular
        qPopular -->|"yes"| fCap --> trust
        qPopular -->|"no"| trust
        trust --> tier
    end

    subgraph stThreat["Threat type: first match wins"]
        direction TB
        qMalware{"Malware<br/>evidence?"}
        qCapped{"Cap reason<br/>found?"}
        qSocial{"Social-<br/>engineering<br/>evidence?"}
        qUnwanted{"Unwanted-<br/>content<br/>evidence?"}
        tMalware["malware"]
        tSocial["social_engineering"]
        tUnwanted["unwanted_software"]
        tNone["none"]
        qMalware -->|"yes"| tMalware
        qMalware -->|"no"| qCapped
        qCapped -->|"yes"| tNone
        qCapped -->|"no"| qSocial
        qSocial -->|"yes"| tSocial
        qSocial -->|"no"| qUnwanted
        qUnwanted -->|"yes"| tUnwanted
        qUnwanted -->|"no"| tNone
    end

    stHeur --> stScore --> stCap --> stThreat
```

<sub>🖼️ Static image (for viewers without Mermaid): [`docs/architecture/img/risk-scoring.png`](docs/architecture/img/risk-scoring.png)</sub>

Evidence used by the threat-type step (`malware_evidence`, `social_evidence` and `unwanted_evidence` in
`app/scoring.py`):

| Threat type | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `malware` | Listed as malware by an engine (URLhaus), or the URL path ends in an executable or archive extension (`.exe`, `.apk`, `.zip`, ...) and the verdict is not legitimate |
| `social_engineering` | Listed as phishing by an external engine or feed, impersonates a brand (and is not a defensive redirect), has a login/password form while the verdict is not legitimate, or the verdict is phishing |
| `unwanted_software` | Parked domain, SEO spam or hidden iframe, or a spam-blocklist listing when the verdict is not legitimate |
| `none` | None of the above, or the domain has a popular/official cap reason |

### 5. Database ER diagram

There are 11 tables in one SQLite file (stdlib `sqlite3`, WAL mode, one connection per thread). `SCHEMA` in
`app/db.py` creates the v1 tables. `migrate()` adds the v2 columns (marked "v2") and the `scan_dom` table, and it is
safe to run more than once. The relationships are kept by the application code only: SQLite foreign keys are turned
off and no `REFERENCES` clauses are declared. `scans.data` holds the complete `ScanResult` JSON, and the other
`scans` columns are indexed copies used for filters, pivots and analytics.

```mermaid

        INTEGER id PK
        TEXT url
        TEXT normalized_url
        TEXT domain "indexed"
        TEXT registered_domain "indexed"
        TEXT tld
        TEXT created_at "ISO-8601 UTC"
        INTEGER duration_ms
        TEXT source "web, api, bulk, text, qr, watch, extension"
        TEXT verdict "legitimate, suspicious, phishing"
        INTEGER risk_score "0-100"
        REAL confidence
        REAL ml_prob
        REAL heuristic_score
        TEXT brand
        TEXT country_code

        TEXT tags "JSON list"
        TEXT notes
        TEXT data "full ScanResult JSON"
        TEXT ip "v2"
        TEXT asn "v2"
        TEXT registrar "v2"
        INTEGER trust_score "v2"
        TEXT tier "v2"
        TEXT threat_type "v2"
        TEXT category "v2"
        TEXT tested_depth "v2: full or lexical"
    }
    SCAN_DOM {
        INTEGER scan_id PK, FK
        BLOB html_gz "gzip, max 500 KB"
        INTEGER size
        INTEGER truncated
        TEXT source
        TEXT created_at
    }
    REPORTS {

        TEXT domain

    }

    WATCHLIST {

    SCANS ||--o| SCAN_DOM : "DOM snapshot"
```

### 6. Deployment: local vs Vercel

On a laptop, `./start.sh` starts two processes. The first is `uvicorn` on port 8000, which runs the API, the 60 s
watchlist scheduler and the startup demo seed. The second is the Vite dev server on port 5173, which proxies the API
paths to port 8000. The Chrome extension talks to port 8000 directly. The hosted demo (Vercel project
`phishguard-mini-project`, region `bom1`) serves the built SPA from the CDN and runs the *unchanged* FastAPI app
inside one Python function through `deploy/cloud_app.py`. On a cold start, that wrapper copies the bundled
`deploy/seed.db` to `/tmp`, so demo data resets on every cold start. The scheduler is off in the cloud, and a daily
Vercel Cron call to `/api/_cron` does the watchlist re-checks and data retention instead.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph local["Local development: ./start.sh"]
        startSh["start.sh: creates backend/.venv (uv or venv),<br/>npm install, trains the model if metrics.json is missing"]
        viteDev["Vite dev server on :5173<br/>React SPA with hot reload"]
        uvicornApi["uvicorn app.main:app on :8000<br/>FastAPI + 60 s scheduler + demo seed"]
        localDb[("backend/data/phishguard.db<br/>SQLite, WAL mode")]
        localFeeds["backend/data/feeds/<br/>downloaded on startup if empty"]
        chromeExt["Chrome extension<br/>calls localhost:8000"]
        devBrowser["Browser on localhost:5173"]
        startSh --> viteDev
        startSh --> uvicornApi
        devBrowser --> viteDev
        viteDev -->|"proxy /api/, /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json,<br/>/static, /screenshots"| uvicornApi
        chromeExt --> uvicornApi
        uvicornApi --> localDb
        uvicornApi --> localFeeds
    end

    release["Release steps<br/>deploy/build_cloud_seed.py (seed.db + feeds/*.gz),<br/>deploy/preflight.py, vercel deploy --prod"]

    subgraph vercel["Vercel: project phishguard-mini-project, region bom1"]
        vBuild["Build: npm ci --prefix frontend,<br/>cd frontend && npm run build"]
        vCdn["Static frontend/dist on the CDN<br/>/assets/* cached for 1 year"]
        vRewrites{"vercel.json rewrites"}
        vFunction["Python function api/index.py<br/>deploy/cloud_app.py wraps the unchanged app.main<br/>root requirements.txt, maxDuration 300 s"]
        vCold["Cold start: seed.db copied to /tmp/phishguard.db,<br/>feeds/*.gz unpacked, feeds_index.pkl.gz injected,<br/>Tranco .npz preloaded, models warmed up"]
        vTmpDb[("/tmp/phishguard.db<br/>per instance, reset on cold start")]
        vCron["Vercel Cron 30 2 * * * (02:30 UTC)<br/>/api/_cron: up to 5 watchlist checks + retention"]
        visitor["Visitor's browser"]
        vBuild --> vCdn
        visitor --> vRewrites
        vRewrites -->|"/api/*, /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json"| vFunction
        vRewrites -->|"other paths: SPA fallback to index.html"| vCdn
        vFunction --> vCold --> vTmpDb
        vCron --> vFunction
    end

    localDb -.->|"snapshot"| release
    release -.->|"upload"| vBuild
```

### Components

**Backend API** ([`backend/app/main.py`](backend/app/main.py)): creates the FastAPI app (Swagger UI at `/docs`, ReDoc at `/redoc`, CORS open for the extension) and registers the routers. On startup it creates and migrates the SQLite schema, back-fills newer fields on old rows, downloads the threat feeds if none are loaded, seeds demo data into an empty database (unless `PHISHGUARD_NO_SEED=1`), starts the watchlist scheduler (unless `PHISHGUARD_NO_SCHEDULER=1`) and resumes unfinished bulk jobs.

| Router file | Prefix | What it serves |
|---|---|---|
| [`routers/scans.py`](backend/app/routers/scans.py) | `/api` | `POST /scan`; history with filters and pivots; export (CSV/JSON); get, tag/annotate, delete, rescan and compare scans; stored HTML (`/dom`); timeline; per-domain intelligence (`/domains/{domain}`) |
| [`routers/insights.py`](backend/app/routers/insights.py) | `/api` | Relationship graph, similar scans (same IP / ASN / registrar), detection funnel |
| [`routers/bulk.py`](backend/app/routers/bulk.py) | `/api/bulk` | Bulk jobs of up to 500 URLs from a JSON list or a CSV/TXT upload |
| [`routers/tools.py`](backend/app/routers/tools.py) | `/api` | URL extraction from email/SMS text, typosquat (look-alike domain) finder |
| [`routers/community.py`](backend/app/routers/community.py) | `/api/reports` | Community reports and voting |
| [`routers/watchlist.py`](backend/app/routers/watchlist.py) | `/api/watchlist` | Monitored URLs/domains, run-now and check history |
| [`routers/misc.py`](backend/app/routers/misc.py) | `/api/...` | Alerts, threat feeds (status, refresh, search), activity log, settings, analytics, health, live stats, demo-data admin |

| Service | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| [`services/scanner.py`](backend/app/services/scanner.py) | The scan pipeline: normalise the URL, run ML + engine + feed lookup concurrently, score, save the scan and its HTML snapshot, log the event, raise an alert for high-risk results |
| [`services/bulk.py`](backend/app/services/bulk.py) | Background asyncio workers, 5 scans at a time per job, progress stored in the database |
| [`services/watcher.py`](backend/app/services/watcher.py) | 60-second scheduler: due watchlist re-checks, typosquat monitoring, change alerts, data retention |
| [`services/community.py`](backend/app/services/community.py) | Reports and votes; a report is verified at a net score of +3 and rejected at -3 |
| [`services/analytics.py`](backend/app/services/analytics.py) | KPIs, time series, distributions, model statistics, performance and funnel for the dashboard |
| [`services/graph.py`](backend/app/services/graph.py) · [`similar.py`](backend/app/services/similar.py) | Relationship graph from stored scans; other domains on the same IP, ASN or registrar |
| [`services/events.py`](backend/app/services/events.py) | Activity log and alerts, each event linked to its scan or domain |
| [`services/filters.py`](backend/app/services/filters.py) · [`settings_service.py`](backend/app/services/settings_service.py) · [`feeds_service.py`](backend/app/services/feeds_service.py) · [`seed.py`](backend/app/services/seed.py) | Shared history/export filters; settings stored in the database (keys masked); background feed refresh; demo data (about 67 scans over 30 days, reports, votes, 3 watchlist items, alerts) |

**Analysis engine** ([`backend/app/analysis/`](backend/app/analysis)): `engine.py` `run_checks()` produces the evidence and the heuristic score. Each lookup has its own timeout, and a failure becomes an `error` check instead of failing the scan.

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`engine.py`](backend/app/analysis/engine.py) | URL parsing, DNS (dnspython), WHOIS (python-whois), GeoIP (ip-api.com, then ipwho.is), TLS handshake and certificate parsing, HTTP probe and HTML analysis (forms, links, iframes, scripts, meta refresh, security headers), optional Google Safe Browsing / VirusTotal lookups, the check list and the heuristic score |
| [`net_safety.py`](backend/app/analysis/net_safety.py) | SSRF guard: every connection to the scanned site, on every redirect hop, must resolve to a public IP on port 80, 443, 8080 or 8443 |
| [`rdap.py`](backend/app/analysis/rdap.py) | RDAP fallback when the `whois` binary is missing or fails (as on Vercel) |
| [`feeds.py`](backend/app/analysis/feeds.py) · [`dnsbl.py`](backend/app/analysis/dnsbl.py) | Local blocklists (OpenPhish, PhishTank, URLhaus, Phishing.Database, Phishing Army); DNS blocklists (Spamhaus DBL/ZEN, SURBL, URIBL, SpamCop) |
| [`popularity.py`](backend/app/analysis/popularity.py) | Tranco top-1M rank from a hashed local index |
| [`brands.py`](backend/app/analysis/brands.py) | Brand impersonation: typosquat, homoglyph, combosquat, subdomain, punycode, path and content techniques |
| [`content.py`](backend/app/analysis/content.py) | Page category, language (with translate link), parked-domain detection, resources, contacted domains, trackers |
| [`typosquat.py`](backend/app/analysis/typosquat.py) · [`text_extract.py`](backend/app/analysis/text_extract.py) | dnstwist-style permutations with async DNS resolution; URL extraction from email/SMS text (including defanged links) |

**Risk scoring** ([`backend/app/scoring.py`](backend/app/scoring.py)): `risk = round(0.6 × ML probability × 100 + 0.4 × heuristic score)`, raised to at least 90 on a blocklist hit and to at least 85 for a verified community report; 35 and 65 (editable in Settings) separate Legitimate, Suspicious and Phishing. It also caps popular and official brand domains when nothing lists them, and sets the trust score (100 − risk), the tier, the threat type, the positive and negative factors and the plain-English summary.

**Machine learning** ([`backend/ml/`](backend/ml)): [`features.py`](backend/ml/features.py) extracts lexical URL features with the same code at training and prediction time; [`train.py`](backend/ml/train.py) builds the dataset, trains Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and SVM, evaluates them and writes [`artifacts/`](backend/ml/artifacts) (`*.joblib` + `metrics.json`); [`predictor.py`](backend/ml/predictor.py) loads the models once, predicts with the best one (Random Forest), returns all four probabilities and the top feature impacts; [`collect_legit.py`](backend/ml/collect_legit.py) optionally samples real legitimate deep links from public sitemaps.

**Database** ([`backend/app/db.py`](backend/app/db.py)): SQLite in WAL mode with tables `scans`, `scan_dom` (gzipped HTML snapshots), `reports`, `votes`, `watchlist`, `watch_checks`, `alerts`, `events`, `bulk_jobs`, `bulk_items` and `settings`.

**Frontend** ([`frontend/src/`](frontend/src)): React 19 + TypeScript, built with Vite and styled with Tailwind CSS. [`App.tsx`](frontend/src/App.tsx) lazy-loads one chunk per page inside a shared [`Layout`](frontend/src/layout/Layout.tsx) (sidebar, quick-scan box, alerts bell, light/dark/system theme, API health dot, demo-mode banner). Data comes through [`api/client.ts`](frontend/src/api/client.ts) and [`api/client_v2.ts`](frontend/src/api/client_v2.ts) with TanStack Query.

| Route | Page | Route | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Overview | `/graph` | Relationship graph |
| `/scan` | Scan (URL, email/SMS text, QR code) | `/model` | Model Lab |
| `/scans/:id` | Scan report (15 tabs) | `/watchlist` | Watchlist |
| `/history` | History | `/typosquat` | Typosquat finder |
| `/domains/:domain` | Domain intelligence | `/community` | Community reports |
| `/bulk`, `/bulk/:id` | Bulk scan | `/feeds` | Threat feeds |
| `/analytics` | Analytics | `/alerts` · `/activity` | Alerts · Activity log |
| `/settings` | Settings | `/api-guide` | API guide |

The report page ([`pages/Report.tsx`](frontend/src/pages/Report.tsx) + [`pages/report/`](frontend/src/pages/report)) has 15 tabs: Summary, ML Explanation, Domain, Geo & Hosting, SSL, HTTP, Content, Resources, Brand, Reputation, Screenshot (a thum.io page image, when enabled in Settings), Source, Graph, Timeline and Raw JSON. Shared components in [`components/`](frontend/src/components) include `RiskGauge`, `VerdictBadge`, `Kpi` (with sparklines), `ChartCard`, `DataTable` (with pagination), `ForceGraph` (d3-force), `Tabs`, `Modal`/`Drawer`, `Toast`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState` and `RangeSelect`.

**Chrome extension** ([`extension/`](extension)): plain JavaScript, Manifest V3. The service worker quick-scans pages as you browse (cached for 30 minutes), colours the toolbar badge, notifies you when a page is flagged as phishing and adds a "Scan link with PhishGuard" context-menu item; for flagged pages it can inject a warning banner (`content/banner.js`); the popup runs a deep scan of the current tab and links to the full report; the options page sets the backend and dashboard URLs and the auto-scan and banner toggles.

**Vercel deployment** ([`api/index.py`](api/index.py), [`deploy/`](deploy), [`vercel.json`](vercel.json)): the static frontend plus one Python function that copies a bundled demo-data snapshot into `/tmp`, runs with `PHISHGUARD_CLOUD=1` (the UI shows a demo banner) and uses a daily Vercel Cron job for watchlist checks.

## 🧰 Tech stack

PhishGuard has three tiers. The clients are a React single-page dashboard and a Chrome extension. In the middle is
a FastAPI REST API that runs a machine-learning URL classifier next to a network analysis engine. All data is kept in
one SQLite database. This section lists every library and external service the project uses, the version that is
actually installed, and why it is there.

**Where the versions come from (checked 2026-10-25).**
Frontend: `frontend/node_modules/<package>/package.json`, which matches `frontend/package-lock.json` (Vercel runs
`npm ci` on that lockfile).
Backend: the packages installed in `backend/.venv` (Python 3.12.13).
The root [`requirements.txt`](requirements.txt) pins the same Python versions for the Vercel function, because
the scikit-learn models have to be loaded by the version that trained them.
[`backend/requirements.txt`](backend/requirements.txt) only sets minimum versions (`>=`) for a fresh local
install.

Related pages: [diagrams.md](docs/architecture/diagrams.md) (7 architecture diagrams) and [api-endpoints.md](docs/architecture/api-endpoints.md) (all
48 REST endpoints).

**Layers:** [Frontend](#frontend) · [Backend](#backend) · [Machine learning](#machine-learning-1) ·
[Analysis / network](#analysis--network) · [Data sources](#data-sources) · [Deployment](#deployment) ·
[Tooling](#tooling)

| Library | Version | Why it is used |

### Machine learning

`backend/ml/` holds training (`python -m ml.train`) and inference (`ml/predictor.py`). On the test set of 29,272
URLs, the Random Forest scores F1 0.8561 and ROC-AUC 0.9449. All numbers are in
[`backend/ml/artifacts/metrics.json`](backend/ml/artifacts/metrics.json).

| Library | Version | Why it is used |
|---|---|---|
| [scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org) | 1.9.1 | The four classifiers: Logistic Regression (with `StandardScaler`), Decision Tree (depth 20), Random Forest (150 trees, the model that decides) and an SVM (Nystroem RBF features + `LinearSVC`, wrapped in `CalibratedClassifierCV` to get probabilities). It also provides the `StratifiedGroupKFold` split by campaign, 5-fold cross-validation and every metric (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, ROC and PR curves, confusion matrix). |
| [NumPy](https://numpy.org) | 2.5.4 | Feature vectors, the perturbation-based explanations (each feature is reset to the legitimate median and the change in probability is measured) and the compact Tranco index (`tranco_index.npz`). |
| [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org) | 3.1.0 | Loads, cleans and joins the training CSVs (PhiUSIIL, PhishTank, Tranco, sitemap links). The predictor passes a DataFrame to models that were fitted on DataFrames. |
| [SciPy](https://scipy.org) | 1.18.1 | Numerical backend of scikit-learn. It has to be installed for the models to unpickle, so it is pinned in the root `requirements.txt`. |
| [joblib](https://joblib.readthedocs.io) | 1.6.0 | Saves and loads the four trained models (`backend/ml/artifacts/*.joblib`, next to `metrics.json`). |
| [tldextract](https://github.com/john-kurkowski/tldextract) | 5.4.0 | Splits a host into sub-domain, domain and public suffix using the Public Suffix List. It is used for the URL features, for the campaign key that keeps each campaign entirely in train or entirely in test, and for the registered domain throughout the engine. |

### Analysis / network

`backend/app/analysis/` is the engine behind the roughly 60 checks of a deep scan. Live requests to the scanned site
go through the SSRF guard in `net_safety.py` first.

| Library | Version | Why it is used |
|---|---|---|
| [httpx](https://www.python-httpx.org) | 0.28.1 | Async HTTP client. It fetches the scanned page (re-checking every redirect hop) and calls RDAP, geo-IP, Safe Browsing and VirusTotal. It also downloads the threat feeds and the Tranco list. |
| httpcore | 1.0.9 | The transport layer under httpx. `net_safety.py` plugs in a guarded network backend that connects only to the public IP that was already checked, so a DNS-rebinding trick cannot redirect the request to an internal address. |
| [dnspython](https://www.dnspython.org) | 2.9.0 | DNS records (A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT), DNSBL queries, and checking which typosquat permutations resolve (`dns.asyncresolver`). |
| [python-whois](https://github.com/richardpenman/whois) | 0.9.6 | WHOIS lookups for domain age, registrar and expiry date. RDAP is the fallback. |
| [Beautiful Soup 4](https://www.crummy.com/software/BeautifulSoup/) (`beautifulsoup4`) | 4.15.0 | Parses the fetched HTML with `html.parser`. Inputs for the checks: forms, password fields, form actions that post to another site, links, hidden iframes, external scripts and the page title. It also feeds the content analysis (category, parked page, trackers, third-party resources). |
| [langdetect](https://github.com/Mimino666/langdetect) | 1.0.9 | Detects the page language. It is seeded, so the result is the same on every run. |
| [mmh3](https://github.com/hajimes/mmh3) | 5.3.1 | 64-bit MurmurHash3 of each of the 1,000,000 Tranco domains. The hashes and ranks are stored as a NumPy index of about 12 MB for fast popularity lookups. |
| `ssl`, `socket`, `ipaddress` (standard library) | Python 3.12 | TLS handshake on port 443 and the certificate checks (HTTPS available, valid, not self-signed, certificate age, expiry). Private, loopback and reserved address detection for the SSRF guard. |
| Project code (no library) | n/a | `typosquat.py` (dnstwist-style look-alike permutations), `text_extract.py` (URLs found in email or SMS text, including defanged `hxxp://` and `example[.]com`), `brands.py` (brand keywords and official domains), `dnsbl.py` (blocklist return codes and hourly test-point checks) and `app/scoring.py` (risk score, tier, threat type). |

### Data sources

The training code reads only frozen snapshots under `backend/ml/data/raw/` and never the live feeds. At scan time
the threat feeds are local files in `backend/data/feeds/`. They are downloaded on first start (when the folder is
empty) and again on `POST /api/feeds/refresh`. The live demo uses a snapshot of them.

| Data source | Version / snapshot | Why it is used |
|---|---|---|
| [PhiUSIIL Phishing URL Dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/967/phiusiil+phishing+url+dataset) (UCI #967) | CSV release of 2024-03-04 | **Training only:** 45,000 phishing URLs and 40,753 augmented legitimate homepages. |
| [Tranco](https://tranco-list.eu) top-1M list | List of 2026-10-23 | **Training:** the top-30k domains (21,825 augmented legitimate domains) and 6,448 real sub-domain hosts. Ranks 30,001 to 60,000 are kept apart for the held-out "modern" legitimate set. **Scan time:** popularity rank (`popular_site` check) and the popular-domain cap. |
| Public sitemaps of Tranco sites | Collected by `ml/collect_legit.py` | **Training only:** 4,097 real legitimate deep links. Without them, "URL has a path" would look like a phishing signal. |
| [PhishTank](https://phishtank.org) verified-online feed | Snapshot of 2026-10-24, 57,062 entries | **Training:** 16,000 phishing URLs, plus 1,000 held out. **Scan time:** local blocklist. |
| [OpenPhish](https://openphish.com) public feed | Snapshot of 2026-10-24, 300 entries | **Training:** 241 phishing URLs. **Scan time:** local blocklist. |
| [Phishing.Database](https://github.com/mitchellkrogza/Phishing.Database) ACTIVE lists | Snapshot of 2026-10-24, 392,174 entries | **Training:** 12,000 phishing hosts, plus 1,000 held out. **Scan time:** local blocklist. |
| [URLhaus](https://urlhaus.abuse.ch) online list (abuse.ch) | Snapshot of 2026-10-24, 55,475 entries. When abuse.ch answers HTTP 410, it comes from the malware-filter mirror | **Scan time only:** malware-distribution URLs. A hit sets the threat type to `malware`. |
| [Phishing Army](https://phishing.army) blocklist | Snapshot of 2026-10-24, 154,182 domains | **Scan time only:** an additional phishing-domain blocklist. |
| DNSBL zones: Spamhaus DBL, SURBL, URIBL (domains); Spamhaus ZEN, SpamCop (IPs) | Live DNS queries, cached for 1 h | Spam and abuse reputation (on by default, Settings → `enable_dnsbl`). Every zone is tested against its official test point once an hour. If a resolver refuses the queries, the result is "not verifiable", never "clean". |
| WHOIS (port 43) and RDAP via [rdap.org](https://rdap.org) | Live | Domain age, registrar and expiry. RDAP is queried when WHOIS returns no creation date (Settings → `enable_rdap`). |
| [ip-api.com](https://ip-api.com) and [ipwho.is](https://ipwho.is) | Live, free tiers | Geo-IP of the server: country, city, ISP, AS number and a hosting flag. ipwho.is is the fallback when ip-api.com rate-limits (45 requests/min). |
| [Google Safe Browsing](https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing) v4 and [VirusTotal](https://www.virustotal.com) API v3 | Optional, needs an API key | Extra reputation engines. They run only when a key is entered in Settings, and they are off on the live demo. |
| [thum.io](https://www.thum.io) | Live image service | Powers the report's **Screenshot** tab. When Settings → `enable_screenshots` is on (it is off by default), the scan saves an `image.thum.io/get/width/1200/crop/800/noanimate/<url>` link. The browser then loads the thumbnail directly from thum.io. |
