## 🤖 Machine learning

PhishGuard's ML layer reads **only the URL string**. It needs no network access, so it works offline, cannot be fooled by cloaking, and returns a prediction in milliseconds. Four classic scikit-learn classifiers are trained on the same **44 lexical features**. All four give a probability for every scan, and the best one, **Random Forest**, supplies the phishing probability that makes up 60% of the [risk score](#-risk-scoring).

> [!NOTE]
> Every number in this section comes from [`backend/ml/artifacts/metrics.json`](backend/ml/artifacts/metrics.json): model version **`2026.10.24-1812`**, trained 2026-10-24 18:12 UTC. The full training run took **100.3 s**. The same file feeds the **Model Lab** page (`/model`) and `GET /api/analytics/model`, so the README, the UI and the API always show the same results.

### Datasets

All training data is read from **local snapshots** in `backend/ml/data/raw/` (never from live feeds), so a training run can be repeated exactly.

| Class | Source | URLs in training set | What it contributes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 🎣 Phishing | [PhiUSIIL Phishing URL Dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/967/phiusiil+phishing+url+dataset) (UCI #967, label 0 = phishing) | 45,000 | Large academic corpus (only 45% of its phishing URLs use HTTPS) |
| 🎣 Phishing | [PhishTank](https://phishtank.org/) verified-online feed (snapshot 2026-10-24) | 16,000 | Recent, human-verified phishing URLs |
| 🎣 Phishing | [Phishing.Database](https://github.com/mitchellkrogza/Phishing.Database) ACTIVE list | 12,000 | Current phishing hosts |
| 🎣 Phishing | [OpenPhish](https://openphish.com/) community feed | 241 | Very fresh phishing URLs |
| ✅ Legitimate | PhiUSIIL legitimate domains, augmented | 40,753 | Broad set of real sites |
| ✅ Legitimate | [Tranco](https://tranco-list.eu/) top-30k domains, augmented | 21,825 | Popular sites |
| ✅ Legitimate | Real human-facing sub-domains from the Tranco list (`docs.`, `shop.`, `login.` ...) | 6,448 | Legitimate sub-domain hosts |
| ✅ Legitimate | Real deep links from the public sitemaps of Tranco top-30k domains | 4,097 | Real article, product and docs URLs |
| | **Total** | **146,364** | **73,241 phishing / 73,123 legitimate** (almost exactly 50/50) |

**Split.** `StratifiedGroupKFold` makes an **80/20 split: 117,092 train / 29,272 test**. The groups are campaign keys (phishing) or domains (legitimate), so no campaign or domain is in both train and test. Five-fold cross-validation inside the training part uses the same grouping.

**Realistic held-out set (`modern_eval`).** There is also a separate set of **4,000 URLs** that is never used for training or model selection inside a variant:

| Part | Size | How it is kept unseen |
|---|---:|---|
| PhishTank URLs | 1,000 | Their whole campaign keys are removed from training |
| Phishing.Database URLs | 1,000 | Their whole campaign keys are removed from training (hosts left bare, as published) |
| Legitimate sitemap deep links from Tranco ranks 30,001-60,000 | 2,000 | Every domain in that rank range is excluded from the legitimate training data (at most 2 URLs per domain) |

### Data cleaning and bias handling

Phishing and legitimate URLs come from very different places (threat feeds against popularity lists), so a naive model learns *how the data was collected* instead of *what phishing looks like*. [`backend/ml/train.py`](backend/ml/train.py) removes these shortcuts:

| Problem | Fix in `train.py` |
|---|---|
| **Duplicate campaigns.** One kit is often deployed on hundreds of URLs of the same domain, and feeds overlap. | Phishing URLs are deduplicated across all sources (scheme ignored) and **capped at 3 URLs per campaign key**. The key is the registered domain, PSL-private-aware, or the tenant host on free-hosting platforms such as `x.vercel.app`. |
| **Legitimate = bare homepages.** Every PhiUSIIL legitimate URL is a bare `https://www.<domain>`, so "has a path" would look like phishing. | Legitimate hosts are augmented: `www.` is toggled, **about 40% get a realistic synthetic deep-link path** (about 15% of those carry a query string), and about 10% of bare domains get a common sub-domain. They are mixed with **real sitemap deep links (max 6 per domain)** and **real sub-domain hosts (45% given a path)**. |
| **Phishing.Database = bare hosts.** The list has hosts only, so "no path" would look like phishing. | Their scheme is filled in at **PhishTank's HTTPS rate (0.93)**, and **41% of the training hosts** (PhishTank's own path rate) borrow the path and query of a random *training* PhishTank URL. Hosts that are a Tranco top-100k site or an official brand domain are dropped as probable feed false positives. |
| **Label noise in the legitimate class.** | A legitimate URL is dropped if its host also appears in any phishing source, sits on a free-hosting platform, or is a URL shortener. |
| **Train/serve skew.** | Every URL is normalised the same way in training and at prediction time: trimmed, lower-cased, default scheme added, trailing slash removed (`normalize_url` in [`features.py`](backend/ml/features.py)). |
| **HTTPS bias** | See [the HTTPS-bias fix](#the-https-bias-fix) below: the scheme is not a model input at all. |

An optional `--balance-strata` mode (equal phishing and legitimate counts per path-depth and query stratum) was also evaluated. It did not improve the realistic set, so it is off by default.

### The 44 lexical features

[`backend/ml/features.py`](backend/ml/features.py) computes 45 features from the URL string. `uses_https` is shown in the report but is **not** a model input, so the model uses **44**. Brand checks work on token and label boundaries with an allowlist of official brand domains, so `purchase.com` does not match "chase" and `googleusercontent.com` is not flagged.

| Group | # | Features | Share of RF importance |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| 📏 Length | 4 | URL length (without scheme), hostname length, path length, query-string length | 14.6% |
| 🔣 Character counts | 11 | dots, hyphens, underscores, `@`, `?`, `=`, `&`, slashes, other special characters (`~+!*,;$%`), digits, digit ratio | 12.7% |
| 🌐 Host structure | 9 | digits in host, hyphens in host, number of sub-domains, sub-domain length, registered-domain length, TLD length, raw IP host (also hex/decimal IPs), punycode `xn--` host, explicit port | 30.5% |
| 🎲 Randomness | 6 | domain entropy, domain vowel ratio, URL entropy, longest token, average token length, long hex/random token | 17.9% |
| 🧭 Path and query | 5 | path depth, number of query parameters, suspicious file extension (`.php`, `.exe`, `.zip` ...), percent-encoded characters, `//` inside the path | 5.7% |
| 🚩 Known-bad lists | 4 | suspicious keywords (`login`, `verify`, `wallet`, `kyc` ... 63 words plus 7 phrases such as `wp-admin`), abused TLD (77, such as `.xyz`, `.top`, `.tk`), URL shortener (51 services), free hosting or user-content platform (132 suffixes plus S3 buckets) | 17.8% |
| 🎭 Brand and deception | 5 | brand outside its official domain, brand in a sub-domain of an unrelated domain, look-alike brand (leet such as `amaz0n`, `rn` for `m`, a one-letter typo; 113 brands), embedded domain (`apple.com.evil.ru`), `http` token inside the host or path | 0.8% |

**Top 10 Random Forest features** (Gini importance from `metrics.json`):

| Rank | Feature | Importance | |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Subdomain length | 15.8% | `████████████████████` |
| 2 | Free hosting / user-content platform | 10.3% | `█████████████` |
| 3 | Hostname length | 7.0% | `█████████` |
| 4 | Suspicious / abused TLD | 6.1% | `████████` |
| 5 | URL entropy | 5.8% | `███████` |
| 6 | Digits in hostname | 4.4% | `██████` |
| 7 | Domain name entropy | 3.8% | `█████` |
| 8 | Number of subdomains | 3.6% | `█████` |
| 9 | Path depth | 3.5% | `████` |
| 10 | URL length (excluding scheme) | 3.5% | `████` |

Brand features carry little weight in the forest because they are rare in the data (5% of phishing URLs). Brand abuse, raw IP hosts and punycode are rare but strong signals, so the live engine handles them with its own hard rules (score floors of 50-85, see [Risk scoring](#-risk-scoring)).

### The four models

All four are built in `make_models()` in [`train.py`](backend/ml/train.py) with `random_state = 42`, trained on the same 44 features, and saved to `backend/ml/artifacts/*.joblib`:

| Model | Exact scikit-learn setup | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Logistic Regression** | `make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=3000))` | Linear baseline, features standardised |
| **Decision Tree** | `DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=20, min_samples_leaf=5)` | Single interpretable tree |
| **Random Forest** ⭐ | `RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=150, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=-1)` | 150 trees; set to single-threaded (`n_jobs = 1`) when served, for low latency on one URL |
| **Support Vector Machine** | `CalibratedClassifierCV(make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), Nystroem(gamma=0.03, n_components=500), LinearSVC(C=1.0, dual=False, max_iter=5000)), method="sigmoid", cv=3)` | RBF kernel approximated with 500 Nyström components; sigmoid (Platt) calibration gives probabilities; fitted on a stratified **40,000-row subsample** to keep training time reasonable |

29,272 URLs from campaigns and domains that never appear in training. The decision threshold is a probability of 0.5. "CV F1" is the 5-fold grouped cross-validation F1 on the training part (mean ± standard deviation).

| Decision Tree | 84.93% | 91.16% | 77.40% | 83.72% | 0.9206 | 83.69% ± 0.27 | 0.466 s |
| **Random Forest** ⭐ | **86.38%** | 90.80% | **80.98%** | **85.61%** | **0.9449** | **85.50% ± 0.23** | 1.551 s |
| Support Vector Machine | 84.58% | 91.00% | 76.78% | 83.29% | 0.9327 | 83.73% ± 0.16 | 8.817 s |

### The HTTPS-bias fix

"HTTP means phishing" was true years ago. It is not true now: free TLS certificates and free hosting platforms serve HTTPS by default. The training data still carries the old pattern:

| Share of URLs using HTTPS | Value |
|---|---:|
| Phishing URLs in the training data | 62.7% |
| ↳ PhiUSIIL phishing (older academic corpus) | 45.4% |
| ↳ PhishTank / Phishing.Database / OpenPhish | 88.5% / 93.1% / 63.5% |
| Legitimate URLs in the training data | 92.5% |
| **Phishing URLs in the realistic held-out set** | **90.3%** |
| Legitimate URLs in the realistic held-out set | 97.8% |

A model that can see the scheme learns the shortcut "no HTTPS means phishing". That gives every modern HTTPS phishing page a free "looks safe" bonus. So `train.py` trains **two feature variants** of all four models and compares them on the realistic set:

| Model | Test F1 with `uses_https` (45 features) | Test F1 without (44) | Realistic F1 with | Realistic F1 without | HTTPS-phishing recall with | HTTPS-phishing recall without |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Logistic Regression | 89.25% | 80.45% | 86.96% | 88.00% | 77.89% | **82.11%** |
| Decision Tree | 91.82% | 83.72% | 85.23% | 83.89% | 82.88% | **83.38%** |
| **Random Forest** | 93.42% | 85.61% | 86.48% | 86.16% | 83.71% | **84.82%** |
| Support Vector Machine | 91.45% | 83.29% | 85.84% | 86.37% | 80.61% | **83.38%** |

- With the scheme, test F1 is about 8 points higher, but almost all of that gain disappears on the realistic set. That shows it was the shortcut, not real skill.
- Without the scheme, **every model catches more HTTPS phishing**, which is the case that matters today.
- Selection rule in `main()`: take the best model of each variant by test F1, and **keep the scheme-free variant unless its realistic F1 is more than 0.5 points lower**. Random Forest without the scheme scores 86.16% against 86.48% with it (0.32 points lower), so the deployed model is the **44-feature, scheme-free** variant (`"feature_variant": "without_scheme"`).
- The scheme is not ignored completely. The live engine still has an `https_scheme` check, but it is only a small heuristic warning (weight 2) instead of a learned shortcut.

### Why Random Forest is the best model

- **Selection rule.** `train.py` picks the model with the highest **test F1**: Random Forest with 85.61%. It also has the highest test accuracy (86.38%), recall (80.98%) and ROC-AUC (0.9449). Its CV F1 of 85.50% ± 0.23 shows the result is stable and not a lucky split.
- **It catches the most phishing where it counts.** On the realistic set it has the highest recall (84.7%), the highest HTTPS-phishing recall (84.8%) and 93.3% recall on unseen PhishTank campaigns.
- **It fits the data.** It works directly on mixed counts, ratios and yes/no flags without scaling, learns interactions such as "long sub-domain on a free-hosting platform", and its feature importances drive the Model Lab charts.
- **The honest trade-off.** Logistic Regression has the fewest false positives on the realistic set (4.1% against 11.9%) and SVM a slightly higher realistic F1 (86.37% against 86.16%). PhishGuard handles Random Forest's false positives in the scoring layer: the ML probability is only **60%** of the risk score, and popular or official domains with no blocklist hit are **capped at 30** (see [Risk scoring](#-risk-scoring)).

### How the explanations work

Every scan returns the probabilities of all four models plus an explanation of the best model's decision (`predict()` in [`backend/ml/predictor.py`](backend/ml/predictor.py)). It is a **perturbation method** (each feature is put back to a typical value and the change is measured), not a black box:

1. Extract the URL's 44 features.
2. The baseline is a "typical legitimate URL": the **median of every feature over the legitimate training rows**, stored in `metrics.json` as `legit_median`.
3. For each feature whose value differs from that baseline, make a copy of the vector with **only that feature reset to the median**. All copies are scored in one batch call, so this is cheap.
4. **Impact = P(phishing) with the real value - P(phishing) with the baseline value.** A positive impact is shown as **risk**, a negative one as **safe**. Changes below 0.0001 are dropped, and the 10 largest by size are returned.

**Example: `https://www.reddit.com/r/netsec`** (Random Forest gives 52.2%; the other models give Logistic Regression 16.0%, Decision Tree 55.6%, SVM 19.0%):

| Feature | Value | Impact on P(phishing) | Direction |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Number of slashes | 2 | +13.3 pts | 🔴 risk |
| Registered domain name length | 6 | -7.2 pts | 🟢 safe |
| Domain name entropy | 2.25 | -6.8 pts | 🟢 safe |
| Average token length | 3.8 | -2.5 pts | 🟢 safe |
| URL entropy | 3.59 | -1.6 pts | 🟢 safe |
| Path length | 9 | -1.5 pts | 🟢 safe |

The baseline legitimate URL has no path, so the forest finds a deep link a little unusual. This borderline ML result is exactly why PhishGuard never uses the ML probability alone: the live checks and the Tranco-popularity cap bring this scan's final risk to **30 (Legitimate, tier Favorable)**.

The predictor loads the models once, behind a lock. If it finds the artifacts half-replaced during a retrain (feature count in a `.joblib` file not matching `metrics.json`), it tries up to 5 times before giving up.

### Retraining the models

The trained models are committed in `backend/ml/artifacts/`, so retraining is optional:

```bash
cd backend
.venv/bin/python -m ml.collect_legit   # optional, needs internet: real legit deep links from public sitemaps
.venv/bin/python -m ml.train           # about 2 minutes: dataset -> features -> 2 variants x 4 models -> artifacts
```

| Input in `backend/ml/data/raw/` (git-ignored) | Needed |
|---|---|
| `PhiUSIIL_Phishing_URL_Dataset.csv` (UCI #967) | Yes |
| `top-1m.csv`: Tranco list of registered domains | Yes |
| `feeds_snapshot_20261024/` with `phishtank.csv`, `phishing_database.txt`, `openphish.txt` (a copy of `backend/data/feeds/`) | Yes |
| `tranco_sub/top-1m.csv`: Tranco list with sub-domains | Optional |
| `sitemaps/legit_deeplinks*.csv`: output of `ml.collect_legit` | Optional |

- **Outputs:** `ml/data/dataset.csv`, `ml/data/modern_eval.csv`, the four `.joblib` models and `metrics.json`. Every file is replaced atomically, models first and `metrics.json` last, so a running API never loads a mismatched set.
- **Flags:** `--no-save` (train and print the results without replacing the models or `metrics.json`) and `--balance-strata` (the experimental per-stratum balancing described above).
- Restart the API afterwards so it loads the new models. The Model Lab page then shows the new metrics automatically.

## 🧮 Risk scoring

Every scan ends in one **0-100 risk score**. The score blends the ML probability with the live heuristic checks, then applies a few hard rules that a human analyst would apply too: "a blocklisted URL is dangerous no matter what the model says" and "a top-10k site with no blocklist hit is not phishing". The code is in two places: `score_checks()` in [`backend/app/analysis/engine.py`](backend/app/analysis/engine.py) (the heuristic score) and [`backend/app/scoring.py`](backend/app/scoring.py) (the blend, the floors, the cap, the tiers, the threat type and the summary). The flow chart is diagram 4 in [Architecture](#️-architecture).

```text
 URL ─► 44 lexical features ─► Random Forest ──────────► p  (phishing probability, 0-1)
     └► 50+ live checks (fail / warn / pass) ─► heuristic h (0-100, with floors and caps)

 risk = round(0.6 × 100p + 0.4 × h)  ─►  blocklist floor 90  ─►  community floor 85
      ─►  popular / official cap 30  ─►  verdict · tier · trust · confidence
      ─►  engines N/M · threat type · positive / negative factors · AI summary
```

### Step 1: the heuristic score (`engine.py`)

Each check returns `pass`, `warn`, `fail`, `info` or `error` with a weight from 0 to 10 (for example: blocklist hit 10, invalid certificate 8, suspicious JavaScript 7, free hosting 4, missing HTTPS 2). Only failures and warnings count:

```text
raw = Σ weight(fail) + 0.4 × Σ weight(warn)
h   = 100 × (1 − e^(−raw / 18))
```

The exponential curve saturates, so many small warnings cannot add up to more than 100, and the first strong signals count most:

| raw | 2 | 5 | 10 | 18 | 25 | 36 | 54 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **h** | 10.5 | 24.3 | 42.6 | 63.2 | 75.1 | 86.5 | 95.0 |

**Floors.** Some single signals are strong enough to set a minimum heuristic score, whatever the sum says:

| Signal | Minimum h |
|---|---:|
| Listed on a threat-intelligence feed or by Google Safe Browsing / VirusTotal | **92** |
| Impersonates a brand **and** the page has a login form | 85 |
| Password form posts to an external domain (`password_external`) | 80 |
| Brand impersonation (`brand_impersonation`) | 75 |
| Malicious JavaScript patterns (`suspicious_js`) | 60 |
| Raw IP address as host · domain younger than 30 days (`domain_age`) | 55 |
| Excessive or cross-domain redirects (`redirects`) · punycode homograph (`punycode`) | 50 |
| Invalid SSL certificate (`ssl_valid`) | 45 |
| High-risk TLD (`suspicious_tld`) | 35 |

**Caps** (applied after the floors):

- **≤ 15** for an official brand domain (for example `paypal.com`), unless it is blocklisted or is a user-content host such as `docs.google.com`.
- **≤ 20** for a Tranco top-10,000 site, unless it is blocklisted or has a hard failure: brand impersonation, off-site password form, suspicious JavaScript, DNS-blocklist listing, or a host that resolves to a private network.

The result is rounded and clamped to 0-100. Every floor and cap that was applied is listed in the report as a `score_reason`.

### Step 2: blend and floors (`compute_score`)

```text
risk = round( 0.6 × (ML probability × 100)  +  0.4 × h )
risk = max(risk, 90)   if the URL is listed by any feed or API engine   (BLACKLIST_FLOOR)
risk = max(risk, 85)   if a community report is verified                (COMMUNITY_FLOOR)
risk = clamp(risk, 0, 100)
```

- The ML probability comes from the best model (Random Forest). The other three models are shown for comparison but do not change the score.
- A community report is **verified** when phishing votes minus legitimate votes reach **3 or more**. The reporter's own label counts as the first vote.
- The report shows this as a **score breakdown** (one line each for the ML model, heuristic checks, blacklists and community, plus the cap line from step 3). Each line shows the component's score, its weight and its contribution in points.

### Step 3: popular / official domain cap (`finalize`)

If the risk is above **30**, it is lowered to **30** and the verdict is recomputed, but only when **all** of these are true:

1. No feed, API engine or DNS blocklist lists the URL, no verified community report exists, and there is no malware evidence.
2. The domain is an **official brand domain** (and the `brand_official` check did not warn), **or** it is **popular**: Tranco top-1k or top-10k tier, rank 1-10,000, or a passing `popular_site` check, with no failing brand-impersonation check.
3. The host is **not a hosting, user-content or shortener platform** (114 suffixes such as `vercel.app`, `github.io`, `pages.dev`, `docs.google.com` and `bit.ly`). Anyone can publish there, so the platform's popularity says nothing about the page.

A capped result adds a line to the breakdown (for example `Popular site (Tranco rank #102) with no blocklist hit: risk capped at 30`, contribution −4) and gets a confidence of at least 0.8.

### Step 4: verdict, tier, trust score and confidence

The two thresholds are **suspicious = 35** and **phishing = 65** by default. They are the only scoring parameters you can change at run time: use the **Settings** page or `PUT /api/settings` (`suspicious_threshold`, `phishing_threshold`, each 0-100, and suspicious must be lower than phishing). They apply to every scan scored after the change. The weights (0.6 / 0.4), floors (90 / 85), the cap (30) and the Trusted limit (15) are constants in `scoring.py`.

| Risk score | Verdict | Trust tier | Tier rule (S = suspicious, P = phishing threshold) | Trust score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-14 | ✅ Legitimate | 🟢 **Trusted** | `[0, 15)` | 86-100 |
| 15-34 | ✅ Legitimate | 🟩 **Favorable** | `[15, S)` | 66-85 |
| 35-49 | ⚠️ Suspicious | 🟡 **Neutral** | `[S, (S+P)/2)` | 51-65 |
| 50-64 | ⚠️ Suspicious | 🟠 **Questionable** | `[(S+P)/2, P)` | 36-50 |
| 65-100 | 🚨 Phishing | 🔴 **Untrusted** | `[P, 100]` | 0-35 |

- **Trust score** = `100 − risk`.
- **Confidence** (0-1) measures how far the score is from the nearest threshold, relative to the width of its band:
  - phishing band: `(risk − P) / (100 − P)`
  - suspicious band: `min(risk − S, P − risk) / ((P − S) / 2)`
  - legitimate band: `(S − risk) / S`

  It is at least **0.9** when a blocklist or a verified community report decided the result, and at least **0.8** for a legitimate popular or official domain that qualifies for the cap.
- **Untested handling.** `tested_depth` is `lexical` when only the URL-based checks, the local feeds and the ML model ran. That happens with a quick scan (`"deep": false` in the API), with network checks turned off in Settings, or when the [SSRF guard](#safety) blocked the target. The score is still computed, but the UI shows **"Untested (lexical only)"** next to the tier and the summary says the live site was not tested. A low score never looks like a full clean bill of health.

### Step 5: detection engines, the "N/M engines" badge

Each report lists every reputation source as an **engine**:

| Engine group | Engines |
|---|---|
| Local threat feeds (always, offline) | OpenPhish, URLhaus (malware), Phishing.Database, PhishTank, Phishing Army |
| Optional cloud APIs (when an API key is set) | Google Safe Browsing, VirusTotal |
| DNS blocklists (network checks on) | Spamhaus DBL, SURBL, URIBL (domain) · Spamhaus ZEN, SpamCop (IPv4 address) |
| PhishGuard itself | **PhishGuard ML**: listed when the *final* verdict is phishing |

**N/M** = engines that list the URL / engines that gave a definite answer. Engines that errored or did not apply are left out of M. The badge and the summary include PhishGuard ML. The "Not listed by any reputation engine" / "Flagged by reputation engines" factor counts **external engines only**, so PhishGuard never vouches for itself.

### Step 6: threat type

The first type with evidence wins: **`malware` > `social_engineering` > `unwanted_software` > `none`**.

| Threat type | Evidence (any one is enough) |
|---|---|
| `malware` | Listed by a malware engine (URLhaus) · the verdict is not legitimate and the URL path ends in an executable or archive (`.exe .apk .scr .bat .cmd .msi .jar .vbs .ps1 .dll .hta .zip .rar .7z .iso .dmg`) |
| `social_engineering` | Listed by a phishing feed or engine · impersonates a brand (not a defensive redirect) · login or password form on a site whose verdict is not legitimate · phishing verdict |
| `unwanted_software` | Parked domain · SEO spam · hidden iframe · listed on a spam blocklist while the verdict is not legitimate |
| `none` | No evidence. Always `none` for a popular or official domain that qualifies for the cap, unless malware evidence exists. |

The report shows the evidence list (`threat_reasons`) next to the type.

### Step 7: positive and negative factors and the AI summary

**Factors** (`factors_for`). Every failing or warning check becomes a **negative factor** with a severity:

- a failure with weight ≥ 6 is **high**, weight ≥ 3 is **medium**, otherwise **low**;
- a warning with weight ≥ 7 is **medium**, otherwise **low**.

A passing check with weight > 0 (or a strong one such as a valid certificate, an old domain or no blocklist listing) becomes a **positive factor**. Three synthetic factors are added:

- the ML probability: under 30% is positive; 50% or more is negative, with high severity at 85% or more and medium at 70% or more;
- the external-engine ratio;
- the cap reason, shown first among the positives.

Negatives are sorted by severity and then weight, positives by weight. The lists are trimmed to 20 negatives and 15 positives.

**AI summary** (`build_summary`). This is plain English produced by **deterministic, rule-based templates**. No external LLM is called, so it works offline and the same scan always gives the same text. It has up to four sentences:

1. The verdict, risk score, trust score and tier.
2. The ML phishing probability and "*N* of *M* detection engines (including PhishGuard ML) flagged it".
3. For a legitimate verdict, the top three **positive signals**. Otherwise, the top three **key findings**: the engine's plain-English facts, most severe first.
4. "Only URL-based (lexical) checks ... the live site is untested" for a lexical scan, or otherwise the threat type.

### Worked example

This is a real scan from the demo data: a phishing kit on a free-hosting platform, `hxxp://www.indesx-mauve.vercel[.]app/` (defanged), with network checks on.

| Step | Input | Calculation | Result |
|---|---|---|---:|
| 1. Failed checks | blocklists 10 · invalid SSL certificate (hostname mismatch) 8 · suspicious JavaScript (obfuscated `eval(unescape(...))`, Telegram bot exfiltration) 7 | 10 + 8 + 7 | 25 |
| 2. Warnings | third-party resources on login page 5 · free hosting 4 · login form 3 · no HTTPS 2 · security headers 2 | 0.4 × 16 | 6.4 |
| 3. Heuristic curve | raw = 31.4 | 100 × (1 − e^(−31.4/18)) | 82.5 |
| 4. Heuristic floors | listed in OpenPhish + Phishing Army → 92 · suspicious JS → 60 · invalid SSL → 45 | max(82.5, 92, 60, 45) | **h = 92** |
| 5. ML | Random Forest P(phishing) = 0.9998 | 0.6 × 99.98 | 59.99 |
| 6. Blend | | 59.99 + 0.4 × 92 = 59.99 + 36.8 = 96.79 → round | 97 |
| 7. Final floors | blocklisted (≥ 90), community report verified with 5 phishing votes to 1 (≥ 85) | max(97, 90, 85) | 97 |
| 8. Cap | listed by feeds, and `vercel.app` is a hosting platform | not applied | 97 |
| **Result** | | 97 ≥ 65 | **Risk 97 · 🚨 Phishing · 🔴 Untrusted** |

- **Trust score** = 100 − 97 = **3**. **Confidence** = (97 − 65) / (100 − 65) = **0.914**.
- **Engines: 3/11 flagged.** OpenPhish, Phishing Army and PhishGuard ML listed it. URLhaus, Phishing.Database, PhishTank and the five DNS blocklists did not. No API keys were set.
- **Threat type:** `social_engineering` ("Listed as phishing by OpenPhish", "Listed as phishing by Phishing Army", "Login/password form on a suspicious site", "Phishing verdict").
- **Summary produced:** *"PhishGuard rates www.indesx-mauve.vercel.app as phishing with a risk score of 97/100 (trust score 3/100, tier Untrusted). The machine-learning model estimates a 100% phishing probability, and 3 of 11 detection engines (including PhishGuard ML) flagged it. Key findings: Listed on threat-intelligence blocklists ...; SSL certificate is not valid ...; Suspicious JavaScript .... Threat type: social engineering (phishing)."*

> [!NOTE]
> **The cap in action:** `https://www.reddit.com/r/netsec/` gets ML probability 0.5216 (a deep link looks a little unusual to the model) and h = 6 (one favicon warning: raw 1.2 → 6.4, and the top-10k cap of 20 does not bind). The blend is round(31.30 + 2.4) = **34**, which is still legitimate but close to the threshold. Reddit is Tranco **#102** with 0/10 external engines listing it, so the cap lowers the risk to **30**. Final result: **Legitimate · Favorable · trust 70 · confidence 0.8**.

### Safety

A phishing scanner has to visit hostile URLs, so the scanner must never be turned into a weapon against its own network. All of this is in [`backend/app/analysis/net_safety.py`](backend/app/analysis/net_safety.py).

**SSRF guard: only public addresses are fetched.**

- **Allowed:** only `http` and `https`, and only ports **80, 443, 8080 and 8443**.
- **Pre-check:** before any live probe the target host is resolved, and **every** resolved address must be globally routable. Refused:
  - loopback, private (RFC 1918), link-local (including the `169.254.169.254` cloud-metadata service), multicast, unspecified, reserved and shared/CGNAT addresses, and IPv6 site-local;
  - IPv4-mapped, 6to4 and NAT64 addresses that wrap a non-public IPv4 address, and Teredo tunnels;
  - local host names (`localhost`, `*.local`, `.internal`, `.lan`, `.corp`, `.home.arpa` ...);
  - IP literals in disguise: decimal `2130706433`, hex `0x7f000001`, octal `0177.0.0.1` and short `127.1` are decoded first.
- **Pinned connections:** the HTTP probe uses a guarded `httpx` client. Its connection layer resolves the host, validates the addresses and then **connects to the validated IP itself** (TLS SNI still uses the host name). A DNS-rebinding answer between "check" and "connect" therefore cannot reach an internal host. The client ignores proxy environment variables.
- **Every redirect re-checked:** automatic redirects are off. `fetch()` follows at most **10** redirects by hand and **re-validates every hop**. A public page that redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` is stopped at that hop. The TLS-certificate check also connects only to a validated address.
- **When a target is blocked:** the live probes are skipped and the report shows `blocked: non-public address` with the reason. The scan still returns a score from the lexical checks, local feeds and the ML model, marked "Untested (lexical only)".
- **What does not use the guard:** fixed third-party lookups (ip-api / ipwho.is geolocation, rdap.org, DNSBL queries, and the thum.io screenshot service for the report's Screenshot tab). Only the host name, IP or URL is sent to them as data, and PhishGuard's server never connects to the target for them.

**Hostile page content is never executed.**

- At most **2 MiB** of the response body is read. The stored DOM snapshot is capped at **500 KB** and kept gzip-compressed in the `scan_dom` table.
- The report's **Source** tab shows the HTML **only as escaped plain text**, line by line in React text nodes. It is never rendered, injected or put in an iframe (there is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or `srcdoc` in the frontend). No form is submitted, and only `GET` requests are made.

**Timeouts everywhere.**

- **Per-request timeout:** `timeout_s`, 8 s by default. It can be set from 0.5 to 60 s, and the engine clamps it to 2-20 s.
- **Per-step limits:** DNS resolution 4 s, cached for 30 s; TCP connect at most 5 s; each DNS-blocklist query at most 2 s; body reads stop at the deadline.
- **Whole scan:** the full set of checks has a hard budget of `max(timeout + 2, 10) + 3` seconds inside the engine, and the scanner adds an outer safety net of `max(25, 2 × timeout + 10)` seconds around it. Every sub-check is wrapped so that a failure or a timeout becomes an `error` check instead of an exception. `run_checks()` and `fetch()` never raise, so one slow or hostile site cannot hang the API.

## 🗂️ Project structure

The repository has three runnable parts: the **FastAPI backend** (detection engine, ML models, REST API), the **React dashboard** and the **Chrome extension**. A small `deploy/` layer runs the same backend on Vercel.

```text
mini-project/
├── api/
│   └── index.py                  # Vercel Python function entry point, imports deploy/cloud_app.py
├── backend/                      # FastAPI service (Python 3.12)
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py               # FastAPI app, startup tasks (feeds, demo seed, scheduler), router registration
│   │   ├── db.py                 # SQLite schema, idempotent migrations, PHISHGUARD_DB_PATH
│   │   ├── scoring.py            # risk score, verdict, trust score, tier, threat type, factors, summary
│   │   ├── routers/
│   │   │   ├── scans.py          # POST /api/scan, history, rescan, tags, compare, export, DOM, timeline
│   │   │   ├── bulk.py           # bulk jobs (JSON list or CSV/TXT upload, up to 500 URLs)
│   │   │   ├── tools.py          # URL extraction from email/SMS text, typosquat finder
│   │   │   ├── community.py      # community reports and votes
│   │   │   ├── watchlist.py      # monitored URLs/domains, manual checks, check history
│   │   │   ├── insights.py       # relationship graph, similar scans, detection funnel
│   │   │   └── misc.py           # alerts, threat feeds, analytics, activity log, settings, health, admin
│   │   ├── services/             # scanner pipeline, bulk workers, watcher, analytics, graph, similar,
│   │   │                         # community, events (activity log + alerts), feeds, settings, demo seed
│   │   └── analysis/
│   │       ├── engine.py         # the 50+ live checks: DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, SSL, HTTP, content, geo, screenshot URL
│   │       ├── brands.py         # brand impersonation (typosquat, homoglyph, combosquat)
│   │       ├── typosquat.py      # dnstwist-style permutation generator
│   │       ├── feeds.py          # OpenPhish, PhishTank, URLhaus, Phishing.Database, Phishing Army
│   │       ├── dnsbl.py          # DNS blocklists (Spamhaus, SURBL, URIBL, SpamCop)
│   │       ├── popularity.py     # Tranco top-1M rank lookup
│   │       ├── content.py        # page category, language, parked pages, resources and trackers
│   │       ├── rdap.py           # RDAP fallback for WHOIS
│   │       ├── net_safety.py     # SSRF guard: blocks private/loopback targets before any fetch
│   │       └── text_extract.py   # URL extraction (incl. defanged hxxp / [.] links)
│   ├── ml/
│   │   ├── features.py           # lexical URL feature extractor (shared by training and prediction)
│   │   ├── train.py              # dataset build, bias handling, training + evaluation of the 4 models
│   │   ├── predictor.py          # loads the models, predicts, explains each prediction
│   │   ├── collect_legit.py      # optional: collects legitimate deep links from public sitemaps

│   │   └── artifacts/            # trained models (*.joblib) + metrics.json (read by the Model Lab)
│   ├── data/                     # runtime data: SQLite DB (git-ignored), threat feeds, Tranco index
│   ├── requirements.txt          # backend dependencies for local development
│   └── README.md

│   └── FE_V2_CONTRACT.md         # frontend data contract
├── scripts/
│   ├── capture_media.py          # screenshot + UI smoke-test generator (Playwright)
│   ├── video/                    # demo video: scenes.json, narration.md, record_demo.py (Playwright + FFmpeg)
│   └── build_readme.py           # joins docs/readme_parts/*.md into README.md with a table of contents
├── requirements.txt              # pinned runtime packages of the Vercel function
├── start.sh                      # one-command local start (API :8000 + dashboard :5173)
├── vercel.json                   # build, rewrites, function settings, daily cron
└── .vercelignore                 # keeps the Vercel upload under 100 MB
```

## 🚀 Getting started

### Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Python** | 3.12 | with `venv` and `pip`, or [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (used automatically by `start.sh` if installed) |
| **Node.js** | 20+ (20.19+ or 22.12+ for Vite 8) | npm comes with it |
| **git** | any recent version | to clone the repository |
| Internet access | | for the live checks (DNS, WHOIS, SSL, HTTP, geo) and threat-feed refreshes |
| `whois` CLI | optional | without it, WHOIS data comes from the RDAP fallback |

The trained models (`backend/ml/artifacts/`), the threat-feed files and the Tranco index are already in the repository, so you do **not** need to download datasets or train anything to run the app.

### Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/at9501264-stack/mini-project.git
cd mini-project
./start.sh
```

Then open:

- 🖥️ **Dashboard:** <http://localhost:5173>
- 📘 **API docs (Swagger UI):** <http://localhost:8000/docs> (ReDoc at `/redoc`)

What `start.sh` does:

1. **First run only:** creates `backend/.venv` (with `uv venv --python 3.12` if uv is installed, otherwise `python3 -m venv`) and installs `backend/requirements.txt`.
2. Trains the models **only if** `backend/ml/artifacts/metrics.json` is missing. It is included in the repository, so this step is normally skipped.
3. **First run only:** runs `npm install` in `frontend/`.
4. Starts the API (`uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000`) and the dashboard (`npm run dev -- --port 5173`) together. **Ctrl+C stops both.**

> [!TIP]
> Two optional packages turn on the **Tranco popularity rank** (`mmh3`) and **page-language detection** (`langdetect`). Without them those two signals show as unavailable and everything else works. Install them once with `backend/.venv/bin/pip install mmh3 langdetect`.

> [!NOTE]
> On the **first start** the API creates `backend/data/phishguard.db` and fills it with demo data in the background (see [Demo data](#demo-data)). Give it about a minute before the charts fill up. `start.sh` needs bash, so on Windows use the manual steps below or WSL.

### Manual setup - macOS / Linux

**Terminal 1 - backend API**

```bash
cd mini-project/backend
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install mmh3 langdetect                    # optional: Tranco rank + page language
uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000               # http://localhost:8000/docs
```

With uv instead: `uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt`.

**Terminal 2 - dashboard**

```bash
cd mini-project/frontend
npm install
npm run dev                                    # http://localhost:5173
```

The Vite dev server proxies `/api`, `/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json`, `/static` and `/screenshots` to the backend, so the dashboard and the API share one origin in the browser.

Other frontend commands:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | TypeScript type-check (`tsc -b`) and production build into `frontend/dist` |
| `npm run preview` | serves the production build (same proxy as `dev`) |
| `npm run lint` | lints the code with oxlint |

### Manual setup - Windows (PowerShell)

**Terminal 1 - backend API**

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/at9501264-stack/mini-project.git
cd mini-project\backend
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install mmh3 langdetect          # optional
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
```

**Terminal 2 - dashboard**

```powershell
cd mini-project\frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>.

> [!TIP]
> If PowerShell refuses to run `Activate.ps1` or `npm` scripts, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned` once. You can also skip activation and call `.venv\Scripts\python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000` directly.

**Retraining is optional.** The raw training data is not in the repository (`backend/ml/data/raw/` is git-ignored). The files to download (the [PhiUSIIL dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/967/phiusiil+phishing+url+dataset), the [Tranco list](https://tranco-list.eu/) and a feed snapshot) and the two commands are listed in [Retraining the models](#retraining-the-models). On Windows, run `.venv\Scripts\python -m ml.train` from the `backend` folder, then restart the API so it loads the new models.

### Environment variables

All variables are optional. The defaults suit local development.

| Variable | Read by | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHISHGUARD_DB_PATH` | backend (`app/db.py`) | `backend/data/phishguard.db` | SQLite database file, created and migrated on startup |
| `PHISHGUARD_NO_SEED` | backend (`app/main.py`) | unset | `1` = do not load demo data into an empty database |
| `PHISHGUARD_NO_SCHEDULER` | backend (`app/main.py`) | unset | `1` = do not start the 60-second watchlist / data-retention loop |
| `PHISHGUARD_CLOUD` | backend (`routers/misc.py`) | unset | `1` = hosted demo mode: `GET /api/health` returns `cloud: true` and the dashboard shows the demo banner |
| `PHISHGUARD_API` | frontend (`vite.config.ts`) | `http://localhost:8000` | backend origin that the Vite dev/preview server proxies to |
| `CRON_SECRET` | Vercel only (`deploy/cloud_app.py`) | unset | if set, `/api/_cron` requires `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` |

Flags accept `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on`. Example - a second backend on another port with an empty database:

```bash
cd backend
PHISHGUARD_DB_PATH=data/test.db PHISHGUARD_NO_SEED=1 .venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001
cd ../frontend && PHISHGUARD_API=http://localhost:8001 npx vite --port 5174
```

Everything else is configured at runtime on the **Settings** page and stored in the database: verdict thresholds (suspicious 35, phishing 65 by default), network checks on/off, page screenshots on/off (off by default; when on, the report's Screenshot tab shows a thum.io preview), the per-check timeout (8 s), data retention (365 days by default, 0 = keep forever) and the optional VirusTotal / Google Safe Browsing API keys (masked in API responses). DNS-blocklist and RDAP lookups can be switched off through `PUT /api/settings` (`enable_dnsbl`, `enable_rdap`).

### Demo data

So the dashboard is never empty, the API seeds demo data **when it starts with an empty database** (no rows in `scans`), unless `PHISHGUARD_NO_SEED=1` is set:

- About **67 scans spread over the last 30 days**, plus community reports and votes, **3 watchlist items** and alerts.
- Every demo scan goes through the normal scan pipeline, so scores, tiers and threat types are computed exactly like a live scan.
- About a dozen well-known sites (Google, GitHub, Wikipedia, ...) get full network scans. The rest are URL + ML only. **Phishing URLs are never fetched.**
- The threat feeds are downloaded in the background if the feed folder is empty. You can refresh them at any time on the **Threat Feeds** page.

Seeding and resetting are exposed under **Admin** in Swagger UI (<http://localhost:8000/docs>):

| Endpoint | Effect |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/admin/seed` | seed status (running, number of demo scans) |
| `POST /api/admin/seed` | loads demo data in the background (skipped if demo data exists, unless `force=true`; `deep=true` runs full network scans on more sites) |
| `POST /api/admin/reset` | deletes scans, reports, votes, watchlist, alerts, events and bulk jobs (**settings are kept**); `reseed=true` loads fresh demo data afterwards |

```bash
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/admin/reset?reseed=true"
```

To start completely from scratch, stop the API, delete `backend/data/phishguard.db*` and start it again.

### Chrome extension

The [`extension/`](extension/) folder is a Manifest V3 extension in plain JavaScript (no build step). It calls the same `POST /api/scan` endpoint as the dashboard.

1. Start the backend on `http://localhost:8000` (and the dashboard on `:5173` if you want the "Open full report" links to work).
2. Open `chrome://extensions` in Chrome or any Chromium browser and switch on **Developer mode**.
3. Click **Load unpacked** and select the `extension/` folder.
4. Pin **PhishGuard** from the puzzle-piece menu so the badge stays visible.

| Feature | How it works |
|---|---|
| **Popup** | "Scan this page" runs a deep scan of the current tab: risk bar, verdict colour, top 3 failed checks, impersonated brand and an "Open full report" link |
| **Auto-scan** | each page you open gets a quick (URL + ML) scan, cached for 30 minutes; the badge shows the risk score in the verdict colour (`!` = backend unreachable) |
| **Phishing alerts** | a desktop notification (click it to open the report) and, if enabled, a red warning banner inside the page |
| **Context menu** | right-click a link, then **Scan link with PhishGuard** |
| **Options** | backend URL, dashboard URL, auto-scan on/off, warning banner on/off (saved in `chrome.storage.sync`) |

By default the extension can only reach `localhost:8000` / `127.0.0.1:8000`. Turning on the in-page banner or saving another backend URL asks Chrome for that extra permission. More details are in [extension/README.md](extension/README.md).

## ☁️ Deployment (Vercel)

The live demo at **<https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app>** (Swagger UI at [`/docs`](https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/docs)) is one Vercel project in region `bom1` (Mumbai). It serves the dashboard as static files and runs the **unchanged FastAPI backend** as a single Python serverless function.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U([Browser]) --> V{{Vercel edge<br/>vercel.json rewrites}}
    V -- "/, /scan, /analytics, ...<br/>(SPA fallback)" --> S[frontend/dist<br/>static React build]
    V -- "/api/*, /docs, /redoc,<br/>/openapi.json" --> F[api/index.py<br/>Python function]
    F --> C[deploy/cloud_app.py<br/>cloud wrapper]
    C --> A[backend/app/main.py<br/>unchanged FastAPI app]
    C -. cold start .-> T[(/tmp/phishguard.db<br/>copy of deploy/seed.db)]
    C -. cold start .-> FD[(/tmp feeds<br/>unpacked deploy/feeds/*.gz)]
    CR([Vercel Cron<br/>02:30 UTC daily]) --> F
```

### Files involved

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| [`vercel.json`](vercel.json) | installs and builds the frontend (`npm ci --prefix frontend`, `cd frontend && npm run build` → `frontend/dist`), rewrites `/api/*`, `/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json`, `/static/*` and `/screenshots/*` to the function and every other path to `index.html`, sets a 300 s function timeout, caches `/assets/*` for a year and defines the daily cron |
| [`api/index.py`](api/index.py) | the Python function entry point; adds the repo root to `sys.path` and exposes `deploy.cloud_app.app` |
| [`deploy/cloud_app.py`](deploy/cloud_app.py) | cloud-only wrapper: sets demo-mode environment defaults, copies the snapshot DB to `/tmp`, makes `backend/data` writable through `/tmp`, unpacks the feeds, warms up models/feeds/Tranco, adds `/api/_diag` and `/api/_cron`, then imports `backend/app/main.py` |
| [`requirements.txt`](requirements.txt) (root) | runtime packages of the function, **pinned to the versions that trained the models** (scikit-learn pickles must be loaded by the same scikit-learn version) |
| [`.vercelignore`](.vercelignore) | keeps the upload under the 100 MB CLI limit: no `node_modules`, `.venv`, raw datasets, local DB, extension, scripts or media |
| [`deploy/build_cloud_seed.py`](deploy/build_cloud_seed.py) | builds `deploy/seed.db` from the local database (removes API keys, closes unfinished bulk jobs, shrinks stored HTML) and packs the threat feeds into `deploy/feeds/*.gz` (31 MB → about 8 MB) plus a prebuilt feed index |
| [`deploy/preflight.py`](deploy/preflight.py) | pre-deploy checks: upload and bundle size, requirements against real imports, snapshot freshness; `--smoke` also starts the cloud app locally and calls `/api/health`, `/api/_diag`, `/api/scans` and a deep scan |

### Step by step

1. **Install the Vercel CLI and log in**

   ```bash
   npm i -g vercel
   vercel login
   ```

2. **Link the repository folder to a Vercel project** (run in the repository root; the existing project is `phishguard-mini-project`)

   ```bash
   vercel link --yes --project phishguard-mini-project
   ```

3. **Refresh the cloud snapshot** from your local demo database and feeds (it never modifies `backend/data`)

   ```bash
   backend/.venv/bin/python deploy/build_cloud_seed.py
   ```

4. **Run the pre-flight checks**. The output must end with `PREFLIGHT OK`.

   ```bash
   backend/.venv/bin/python deploy/preflight.py          # add --smoke for a local rehearsal
   ```

5. **Deploy to production**

   ```bash
   vercel deploy --prod
   ```

   Use `vercel deploy` (without `--prod`) for a protected preview deployment first, then `vercel promote <preview-url>` to put it live.

6. **Verify**

   ```bash
   curl -s https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/api/health     # "status":"ok", "cloud":true
   curl -s -H 'content-type: application/json' \
        -d '{"url":"http://paypal-login-verify.secure-account.xyz/update","deep":true}' \
        https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/api/scan            # verdict "phishing", tier "Untrusted"
   ```

7. **Optional:** add a `CRON_SECRET` environment variable in the Vercel project settings. Vercel then sends it as a bearer token to `/api/_cron`. Without it, the endpoint accepts only Vercel's own cron requests.

No Vercel environment variables are required: `deploy/cloud_app.py` sets its defaults with `os.environ.setdefault`, so any variable you add in the project settings wins.

### Demo mode vs. local run

| | Local (`./start.sh`) | Vercel demo mode |
|---|---|---|
| Database | `backend/data/phishguard.db`, permanent | `/tmp/phishguard.db`, copied from `deploy/seed.db` (70 demo scans) on **every cold start** |
| Your scans, reports, watchlist | kept | kept only until the function instance restarts; two visitors can briefly see different data |
| Demo timestamps | real seed times | shifted forward so the "last 24 h / 7 d / 30 d" charts are never empty |
| Demo seeding | on an empty database | off (`PHISHGUARD_NO_SEED=1`), the snapshot already has the data |
| Watchlist checks + retention | background loop every 60 s | off (`PHISHGUARD_NO_SCHEDULER=1`); a **Vercel Cron job at 02:30 UTC** daily (`/api/_cron`) checks up to 5 due watchlist items and applies retention |
| Threat feeds | downloaded and refreshable | snapshot from the last `build_cloud_seed.py` run, unpacked into `/tmp`; a manual refresh lasts only for that instance |
| WHOIS | `whois` binary, RDAP fallback | RDAP (no `whois` binary on Vercel) |
| VirusTotal / Safe Browsing keys | optional, set on Settings | removed from the snapshot, so these integrations are off |
| UI | normal | `/api/health` reports `cloud: true` and the dashboard shows a "Demo mode" banner |
| Extra route | none | `GET /api/_diag` (runtime diagnostics, cold-start timings) |

The first deep scan on a fresh instance can take a few seconds longer while models and feeds load in the background; typical deep scans take 2-4 s. The demo has no login or rate limiting, so do not enter private data or real API keys there.

The full rehearsal notes, with more verification commands and troubleshooting, are in [docs/DEPLOY_NOTES.md](docs/DEPLOY_NOTES.md).

## 🧭 Usage guide

Open the dashboard (<http://localhost:5173> locally, or the [live demo](https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app)). Every page is in the left sidebar. The header has a **quick-scan box** (URL + ML only, instant), the **alerts bell**, the light/dark **theme toggle** and, at the bottom of the sidebar, the API status dot with the loaded model version.

> [!WARNING]
> Scan suspicious links **in PhishGuard**, never by opening them in your own browser. A deep scan fetches the page from the server, with an SSRF guard that blocks private and local addresses.

### 1. Scan something

The **Scan** page has three input tabs:

| Tab | What you give it | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Single URL** | one link, e.g. `http://paypal-login-verify.secure-account.xyz/update` | **Deep scan on** runs DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, SSL/TLS, HTTP and content checks, brand detection and reputation lookups (2-4 s). **Deep scan off** runs URL features + ML only, in milliseconds. A progress list shows each stage. |
| **Email / SMS text** | a pasted message | every link is extracted, including defanged ones (`hxxp://`, `example[.]com`) and bare domains; tick the ones you want and scan them in one go |
| **QR code** | an image file | the QR code is decoded **in your browser** (jsQR), the URL inside is shown, then scanned |

Every scan opens its **report** at `/scans/<id>`.

### 2. Read a report

The top card summarises the result:

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Risk gauge (0-100)** | `0.6 × ML probability × 100 + 0.4 × heuristic score`, raised to at least 90 on a blocklist hit and at least 85 for a verified community report; very popular official domains are capped unless something lists them |
| **Verdict** | **Legitimate** below 35, **Suspicious** 35-64, **Phishing** 65 and above (thresholds can be changed on Settings) |
| **Trust score** | `100 - risk`, so a high number is good |
| **Tier** | Trusted, Favorable, Neutral, Questionable or Untrusted, a five-band reading of the same score |
| **Threat type** | social engineering (phishing), malware, unwanted software or none, chosen from the evidence |
| **Engines** | how many detection sources flagged the URL (threat feeds, DNS blocklists, optional VirusTotal / Safe Browsing, PhishGuard ML) |
| **Stats row** | confidence, ML probability and model name, failed checks, scan duration, scan time |

Then the tabs, in order:

| Tab | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Summary** | plain-English summary, score breakdown, positive and negative factors, every check grouped by category with pass/fail |
| **ML Explanation** | the phishing probability from each of the 4 models (Random Forest drives the score) and the URL features that pushed it up or down |
| **Domain** | WHOIS/RDAP registrar, creation and expiry dates, domain age, DNS records |
| **Geo & Hosting** | IP addresses, country, ASN and hosting provider |
| **SSL** | certificate validity, issuer, dates and hostname match |
| **HTTP** | status, redirect chain, response headers, security headers |
| **Content** | page title, category, language, forms and password fields, trackers |
| **Resources** | scripts, styles and images the page loads and the domains it contacts |
| **Brand** | impersonated brand and technique (typosquat, homoglyph, combosquat, sub-domain, punycode, ...) |
| **Reputation** | threat-feed hits, DNS-blocklist results, engine list, the community verdict with **Phishing** / **Legitimate** vote buttons |
| **Screenshot** | a page preview from thum.io, when **Capture page screenshots** is on in Settings (off by default) |
| **Source** | the stored HTML of the page |
| **Graph** | this domain's links to IPs, ASNs, name servers, registrars and brands |
| **Timeline** | every event for this scan and domain: scans, rescans, reports, alerts |
| **Raw JSON** | the complete API response |

Header buttons: **Rescan**, **Report** (submit to the community), **Tags & notes**, **Compare** (field-by-field difference with another scan of the same domain), **JSON** download, **Print**, **Share** (copy link) and **Delete**. Click the domain name for the **domain page** (`/domains/<domain>`): every scan of that domain and its risk trend.

### 3. History and pivots

**History** lists every scan with search and filters: verdict, source (web, API, bulk, text, QR, extension), TLD, brand, risk range and date range, plus sorting and paging. The chips in each row are **pivots**: click an IP, ASN, registrar, category, threat type or tier to see every other scan that shares it (the filter is stored in the URL, e.g. `/history?asn=13335`). **Export CSV / JSON** downloads exactly what is filtered.

### 4. Bulk scan

On **Bulk Scan**, paste up to **500 URLs** or upload a **CSV/TXT** file (max 5 MB). The job runs in the background with a progress bar, a verdict pie chart and a results table you can filter and open. Jobs keep running if you leave the page, and an alert is raised when a job finds phishing URLs.

### 5. Watchlist and typosquats

- **Watchlist:** add a URL or domain, a label, a check interval (every 15 minutes, hourly (the default), every 6 hours, daily or weekly; the API accepts 1 minute to 7 days) and optionally **Monitor typosquats**. The background loop runs the first check within about a minute and then re-scans each item when it is due (on Vercel the loop is off and the daily cron does this). **Run** checks an item immediately. Each item shows its check history. You get an alert when the verdict changes or when a new look-alike domain starts resolving.
- **Typosquat:** enter a domain (for example `paypal.com`) to generate dnstwist-style permutations (omission, repetition, transposition, homoglyph, bitsquatting, TLD swap, hyphenation, ...) and check which ones resolve in DNS. A chart compares generated vs. resolving permutations per technique, and any permutation can be quick-scanned with one click.

### 6. Community

On **Community**, report a URL as phishing or legitimate with a comment, and vote on other reports. The reporter's label counts as the first vote. A report becomes **verified** at +3 net phishing votes (its URL then gets a risk of at least 85) and **rejected** at -3. Votes from the Reputation tab of a report land here too.

### 7. Analytics

**Overview** gives the headline view: KPI cards, scans over time, verdict split, risk histogram, top impersonated brands, top hosting countries and a live feed of recent scans. **Analytics** goes deeper, with a range selector (24h / 7d / 30d / 90d / all): scans over time, average risk trend, a weekday × hour heatmap, TLDs, scan sources, impersonation techniques, SSL status, domain age, top failed checks, countries, top domains, threat types, reputation tiers, content categories, the **detection funnel**, throughput and check error rates.

### 8. Model Lab

**Model Lab** shows how the ML part was built and how well it works, all read from `backend/ml/artifacts/metrics.json`: the dataset and its composition, the comparison table of the four models (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, best value highlighted), the metric chart, the **realistic evaluation on unseen domains**, confusion matrices, ROC and precision-recall curves, feature importance and feature statistics (phishing vs. legitimate means).

### 9. Relationship graph

**Graph** draws how scanned domains connect through shared IPs, ASNs, name servers, registrars, brands and redirects (VirusTotal-Graph style). Search for a domain (or open it from a report's Graph tab), choose depth 1 or 2, drag nodes around and click one to see its details and linked scans. Clusters of phishing domains on the same infrastructure stand out quickly.

### 10. Threat feeds, alerts and activity log

- **Threat Feeds:** status and entry counts of the five local blocklists (OpenPhish, PhishTank, URLhaus, Phishing.Database, Phishing Army), charts of top TLDs and targeted brands, a search box across all entries and a **Refresh feeds** button.
- **Alerts:** high-risk scans, verdict changes, new typosquats, bulk jobs that found phishing and community verifications, with severity levels. Mark them read one by one or all at once; the bell in the header shows the unread count.
- **Activity Log:** the full audit trail (scans, rescans, deletions, reports, votes, bulk jobs, watchlist and settings changes, feed refreshes, exports), filterable by type.

### 11. Settings and API

- **Settings:** the suspicious and phishing thresholds (with a live preview of the bands), network checks on/off (off = instant offline URL + ML scoring), page screenshots on/off, the per-check timeout, data retention, and the optional VirusTotal / Google Safe Browsing API keys (stored server-side, masked in responses).
- **API guide** (`/api-guide`) shows ready-to-copy `curl` examples, and **Swagger UI** at [`/docs`](http://localhost:8000/docs) lets you call every endpoint from the browser.

> [!TIP]
> Presenting the project? [docs/DEMO_GUIDE.md](docs/DEMO_GUIDE.md) is a minute-by-minute **5-minute viva demo script**: which URLs to scan, what to point at on each report tab, how to explain the metrics and the risk formula, and short answers to likely questions.

## 🔌 REST API

Everything the dashboard and the Chrome extension do goes through one JSON REST API built with FastAPI, so any script or tool can use the same engine. Every endpoint below can be tried from the browser in the interactive **Swagger UI** at [`/docs`](https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/docs). There is no login and no rate limiting, because this is a demo.

The PhishGuard API (FastAPI, version 2.0.0) has **48 endpoints in 14 routers**. All of them are under `/api`, take
and return JSON, and use ISO-8601 UTC timestamps. There is no authentication, because this is a local / demo
academic project, and CORS allows every origin.

| | Local | Live demo |
|---|---|---|
| API base | `http://localhost:8000/api` | <https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/api> |
| Swagger UI | <http://localhost:8000/docs> | <https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/docs> |
| ReDoc | <http://localhost:8000/redoc> | <https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/redoc> |
| OpenAPI schema | <http://localhost:8000/openapi.json> | <https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/openapi.json> |

Related pages: [diagrams.md](docs/architecture/diagrams.md) (the scan pipeline behind `POST /api/scan` is diagram 2) and
[tech-stack.md](docs/architecture/tech-stack.md).

**How this list was checked (2026-10-25).** The tables below come from `backend/app/routers/*.py` and the
`include_router` loop in `backend/app/main.py`. They were checked against the OpenAPI schema of the imported app
(48 operations) and against the live site's `/openapi.json` (also 48). FastAPI 0.162 wraps included routers, so
`app.routes` lists only the built-in docs routes. Read the schema instead:

```bash
cd backend
PHISHGUARD_NO_SEED=1 PHISHGUARD_NO_SCHEDULER=1 .venv/bin/python -c "
from app.main import app
for path, ops in app.openapi()['paths'].items():
    for method in ops:
        print(method.upper(), path)"
```

### Routers at a glance

The routers are mounted in this order in `backend/app/main.py`:

| # | Router | Source (`backend/app/routers/`) | Prefix | Swagger tag | Endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Scans](#1-scans) | `scans.py`: `router` | `/api` | Scans | 10 |
| 2 | [Domains](#2-domains) | `scans.py`: `domains_router` | `/api` | Domains | 1 |
| 3 | [Insights](#3-insights) | `insights.py`: `router` | `/api` | insights | 3 |
| 4 | [Bulk](#4-bulk) | `bulk.py`: `router` | `/api/bulk` | Bulk | 4 |
| 5 | [Tools](#5-tools) | `tools.py`: `router` | `/api` | Tools | 2 |
| 6 | [Community](#6-community-1) | `community.py`: `router` | `/api/reports` | Community | 4 |
| 7 | [Watchlist](#7-watchlist) | `watchlist.py`: `router` | `/api/watchlist` | Watchlist | 5 |
| 8 | [Alerts](#8-alerts) | `misc.py`: `alerts_router` | `/api/alerts` | Alerts | 3 |
| 9 | [Threat Feeds](#9-threat-feeds) | `misc.py`: `feeds_router` | `/api/feeds` | Threat Feeds | 3 |
| 10 | [Analytics](#10-analytics) | `misc.py`: `analytics_router` | `/api/analytics` | Analytics | 5 |
| 11 | [Activity Log](#11-activity-log) | `misc.py`: `events_router` | `/api/events` | Activity Log | 1 |
| 12 | [Settings](#12-settings) | `misc.py`: `settings_router` | `/api/settings` | Settings | 2 |
| 13 | [System](#13-system) | `misc.py`: `system_router` | `/api` | System | 2 |
| 14 | [Admin](#14-admin) | `misc.py`: `admin_router` | `/api/admin` | Admin | 3 |
| | **Total** | | | | **48** |

Several analytics endpoints take a `range` query parameter: `24h`, `7d`, `30d` (default), `90d` or `all`.

---

### 1. Scans

`scans.py`, `router`, prefix `/api`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/scan` | Scan one URL. Body: `{"url": "...", "deep": true, "source": "web"}`. The ML model and the analysis engine run at the same time, then the risk score and verdict are computed and the full `ScanResult` is stored and returned. With `deep: false`, only the URL-based checks and the ML model run (`tested_depth = lexical`). |
| `GET` | `/api/scans` | Scan history as a paginated list of `ScanSummary` rows. Filters: `q`, `verdict`, `source`, `tld`, `brand`, `min_risk`, `max_risk`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `tag`, `domain`, `blacklisted`. Pivots: `ip`, `asn`, `registrar`, `category`, `threat_type`, `tier`. `verdict`, `source`, `tld`, `category`, `threat_type`, `tier`, `ip` and `asn` accept comma-separated lists. Sorting: `sort` (`created_at`, `risk_score`, `domain`, `duration_ms`, `confidence`, `trust_score`) and `order`. Paging: `page`, `page_size` (default 25). |
| `GET` | `/api/scans/export` | Downloads the scans that match the same filters, up to 10,000 rows. `format=csv` gives the summary columns, protected against spreadsheet formula injection. `format=json` gives the full `ScanResult` objects. |
| `GET` | `/api/scans/{scan_id}` | The full `ScanResult` of one scan. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/scans/{scan_id}` | Updates the tags and notes. Body: `{"tags": ["..."], "notes": "..."}`. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/scans/{scan_id}` | Deletes a scan. |
| `POST` | `/api/scans/{scan_id}/rescan` | Runs the full pipeline again on the same URL (`deep=true` by default). It creates and returns a **new** scan with the tags carried over, so the two scans can be compared. |
| `GET` | `/api/scans/{scan_id}/compare/{other_id}` | Compares two scans. Returns both results and a `diff` list of the fields, check statuses and listed reputation sources that changed. |
| `GET` | `/api/scans/{scan_id}/dom` | The stored HTML of the final page (kept gzipped in `scan_dom`, at most 500 KB). Returns 404 when the scan has no snapshot. |
| `GET` | `/api/scans/{scan_id}/timeline` | Activity-log events for this scan and its domain, newest first. `limit` defaults to 200 (maximum 1000). |

### 2. Domains

`scans.py`, `domains_router`, prefix `/api`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/domains/{domain}` | Domain intelligence: every scan of a host or registered domain, with its risk trend and the latest full result. |

### 3. Insights

`insights.py`, `router`, prefix `/api`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/graph` | Relationship graph of domains, URLs, IPs, ASNs, name servers, registrars, brands, redirects and countries. Pass `scan_id` or `domain` to centre it (`depth` default 1, `limit` default 150). With no parameters it returns a global graph of about 50 recent or high-risk domains. |
| `GET` | `/api/scans/{scan_id}/similar` | The newest scans of other domains that share this scan's IP, ASN or registrar, up to 20 per list. |
| `GET` | `/api/analytics/funnel` | Detection funnel: how many scans reached each stage (Scanned, Reachable, Login/password form, Brand impersonation, Feed listed, Phishing verdict). Takes `range`. It lives in the insights router, even though its path is under `/api/analytics`. |

### 4. Bulk

`bulk.py`, `router`, prefix `/api/bulk`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/bulk` | Creates a bulk job from a JSON list: `{"urls": ["..."], "name": "..."}`, at most 500 URLs. The URLs are scanned in the background, 5 at a time, with `source = bulk`. |
| `POST` | `/api/bulk/upload` | Creates a bulk job from an uploaded CSV file (the `url` column, or the first column) or TXT file (one URL per line), at most 5 MB. Only the first 500 URLs are used, and the response then says `truncated: true`. |
| `GET` | `/api/bulk` | Lists the bulk jobs. |
| `GET` | `/api/bulk/{job_id}` | A job's progress and per-URL results. The dashboard polls it every 2 s while the job runs. |

### 5. Tools

`tools.py`, `router`, prefix `/api`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/extract` | Finds the URLs in pasted email or SMS text (`{"text": "..."}`), including defanged forms such as `hxxp://` and `example[.]com`. |
| `GET` | `/api/typosquat` | Generates dnstwist-style look-alike permutations of `domain` (`limit` default 60) and checks which of them resolve in DNS. |

### 6. Community

`community.py`, `router`, prefix `/api/reports`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/reports` | Submits a community report: `{"url": "...", "label": "phishing" or "legitimate", "brand", "comment", "reporter"}`. The reporter's label counts as the first vote. A background scan starts, and `scan_id` is filled in when it finishes. |
| `GET` | `/api/reports` | Lists the reports (`status`, `q`, `page`, `page_size`). |
| `GET` | `/api/reports/{report_id}` | One report. |
| `POST` | `/api/reports/{report_id}/vote` | Votes `phishing` or `legitimate` (`{"vote": "...", "voter": "..."}`). A report is **verified** when phishing votes minus legitimate votes reach 3, and **rejected** at -3. A named voter can change their vote, while anonymous votes always add. |

### 7. Watchlist

`watchlist.py`, `router`, prefix `/api/watchlist`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/watchlist` | Starts watching a URL or domain: `{"target": "...", "interval_minutes": 60, "monitor_typosquats": false, "label": "..."}`. The interval can be 1 minute to 7 days. The first check runs in the background scheduler within about 60 s. |
| `GET` | `/api/watchlist` | Lists the watched targets with their latest risk score and verdict. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/watchlist/{watch_id}` | Stops watching a target. |
| `POST` | `/api/watchlist/{watch_id}/run` | Runs a check now. It rescans the target (and its typosquats, if enabled) and returns the updated item. |
| `GET` | `/api/watchlist/{watch_id}/history` | The target's past checks: risk score, verdict and typosquats found. |

### 8. Alerts

`misc.py`, `alerts_router`, prefix `/api/alerts`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/alerts` | Alerts raised by high-risk scans, watchlist changes and community verification (`unread`, `severity`, `limit` default 200). |
| `POST` | `/api/alerts/read-all` | Marks all alerts as read. |
| `POST` | `/api/alerts/{alert_id}/read` | Marks one alert as read. |

### 9. Threat Feeds

`misc.py`, `feeds_router`, prefix `/api/feeds`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/feeds` | Status of the five local blocklists (OpenPhish, PhishTank, URLhaus, Phishing.Database, Phishing Army): entries, last update and errors, plus totals. |
| `POST` | `/api/feeds/refresh` | Downloads every feed again in a worker thread. It waits up to 120 s. If the download is still going, it returns `status: running` and finishes in the background. |
| `GET` | `/api/feeds/search` | Searches the feed entries (`q`, `limit` default 100). |

`misc.py`, `analytics_router`, prefix `/api/analytics`. Every endpoint except `model` takes `range`.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/analytics/overview` | The KPI cards: total scans; phishing, suspicious and legitimate counts; detection rate = (phishing + suspicious) / total × 100; average risk and scan time; unique domains; blocklist hits; brands impersonated. Each comes with the % change against the previous period of the same length. |
| `GET` | `/api/analytics/timeseries` | Scans over time, split by verdict, in `hour` or `day` buckets (`bucket`). |
| `GET` | `/api/analytics/distribution` | Distributions: verdicts, risk histogram, TLDs, countries, brands, sources, impersonation techniques, most-failed checks, top domains, a weekday × hour heatmap (UTC), SSL status, domain age, threat types, tiers and categories. |
| `GET` | `/api/analytics/model` | Data for the Model Lab page. From `metrics.json`: the dataset summary and each model's metrics, curves and feature importance. Live figures: predictions made, average probability, how often the other models agree with the Random Forest, and accuracy against decided community reports. |
| `GET` | `/api/analytics/performance` | Scan speed: p50, p95, p99, maximum and average duration, throughput per hour, errors and per-check error rates. |

Sending a masked key value keeps the stored key, and an empty string clears it. |

`misc.py`, `admin_router`, prefix `/api/admin`

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/admin/seed` | Loads the demo data in the background. It does nothing if demo data is already there, unless `force=true`. A dozen well-known sites get full network scans. The rest get URL-only (lexical) + ML scans unless `deep=true`. Phishing URLs are never fetched. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/seed` | Seed status: whether it is running, the last run and the number of demo scans. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/reset` | Deletes scans, reports, votes, watchlist items, alerts, events and bulk jobs, but keeps the settings. `reseed=true` loads the demo data again afterwards. |

### Routes outside the 48

These are not counted above, because they are not part of the PhishGuard API schema:

| Method | Path | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json` | Everywhere | FastAPI's built-in Swagger UI, ReDoc and the OpenAPI schema. |
| `GET` | `/` | Local backend only (port 8000) | Small JSON index that links to `/docs` and `/api/health`. On Vercel, `/` is the dashboard. |
| `GET` | `/api/_diag` | Vercel only (`deploy/cloud_app.py`) | Runtime diagnostics: Python version, cold-start timings, warm-up state, `/tmp`, memory, the seeded database. |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/api/_cron` | Vercel only (`deploy/cloud_app.py`) | Daily Vercel Cron job (02:30 UTC): up to 5 watchlist re-checks plus data retention. When `CRON_SECRET` is set, it requires `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`. |

### Errors

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `404` | Unknown scan, report, alert, bulk job or watchlist item, or a scan without a DOM snapshot. |
| `413` | `POST /api/bulk/upload` file larger than 5 MB. |
| `422` | Validation errors: a URL that is not http/https or has no valid host and TLD, an empty or oversized bulk list, invalid settings (for example a suspicious threshold that is not below the phishing threshold), or bad body fields. |

### Example: scan a URL

`POST /api/scan` takes a JSON body with `url` (required; `http://` is added if the scheme is missing), `deep` (optional, default `true`: run the WHOIS, DNS, SSL, HTTP and content checks; `false` = URL features + ML only) and `source` (optional, one of `web`, `api`, `bulk`, `text`, `qr`, `watch`, `extension`; default `web`).

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://phishguard-mini-project.vercel.app/api/scan \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url": "http://paypal-login-verify.secure-account.xyz/update", "deep": true, "source": "api"}' \
  | jq '{id, verdict, risk_score, trust_score, tier, threat_type, summary}'
```

The response is the full scan result: verdict, `risk_score` (0-100), ML probability and the four model scores with feature explanations, every check with its status, the WHOIS / DNS / SSL / HTTP / content / brand / reputation evidence, and the `id` of the stored report, which the dashboard opens at `/scans/{id}`. Replace the host with `http://localhost:8000` when running locally.

## ⚠️ Limitations & ethics

- **Educational prototype.** PhishGuard was built as a B.Tech mini project and the live site runs on demo data. It gives a preliminary assessment, it is **not a replacement for professional security products**, and its verdicts can be wrong in both directions.
- **The ML model reads only the URL string.** It uses lexical features, so a phishing page on a clean-looking URL (especially on a large trusted platform) can slip through, and an unusual legitimate URL can be flagged. On the held-out realistic set (unseen phishing campaigns and less-popular legitimate sites), the Random Forest on its own catches 84.7% of phishing URLs (it misses about 15%) and flags 11.9% of legitimate deep links, before the live checks and the popularity caps are applied.
- **Live checks depend on third parties.** WHOIS/RDAP, GeoIP, DNS blocklists and feed downloads can rate-limit, time out or be unreachable. A failed lookup is shown as an `error` check and counted in the scan's `coverage` figures (`checks_errored`); it never crashes the scan.
- **Demo-mode limits on Vercel.** Data added on the live site resets when the serverless function restarts, watchlist checks run once a day through Vercel Cron, and some network lookups behave differently from a local run.
- **Safe by design, but use it responsibly.** The scanner refuses private, loopback, link-local and other non-public addresses (SSRF guard, re-checked on every redirect) and only connects on ports 80, 443, 8080 and 8443. PhishGuard fetches suspicious pages from the server so you never need to open them in your own browser, and you should not. Only scan sites you are allowed to check.
- **Third-party terms.** The threat feeds and datasets are used under their own licences and terms (several are free for non-commercial use only).
- **No accounts.** The demo has no user accounts, login or rate limiting, so do not expose a local instance to the internet as-is.

## 🔭 Future scope

The synopsis listed these directions; the table shows what this version already covers and what is left.

| Direction (from the synopsis) | Status in this version | Next step |
|---|---|---|
| **Browser extension** for real-time URL checking | ✅ Chrome Manifest V3 extension (auto quick-scan, badge, context menu, popup deep scan) | Firefox/Edge builds, inline warnings on links inside web-mail pages |
| **Web-page content and HTML analysis** | ✅ HTTP and content checks, page category, language, resources, trackers, stored HTML | Visual similarity of the rendered page to the brand it imitates, analysis of JavaScript-heavy phishing kits |
| **Larger, continuously updated datasets** | 🟡 About 146k labelled URLs from five sources; feeds can be refreshed from the Threat Feeds page | Scheduled retraining on fresh feed data, drift monitoring of the model |
| **Advanced ML and deep learning** | ⏳ Four classical models (LR, DT, RF, SVM) on lexical features | Character-level CNN/LSTM or transformer URL models, gradient boosting, combining URL and page-content features in one model |
| **Mobile application** | 🟡 The dashboard is responsive and works on phones | A native Android/iOS app with share-sheet scanning of links from SMS and messengers |
| **Threat-intelligence integration** | ✅ Five local feeds, DNS blocklists, optional Google Safe Browsing / VirusTotal keys | More sources (for example abuse.ch ThreatFox), sharing confirmed community reports back to public feeds |
